title: U.S. chipmaker AMD to invest $400 million in India by 2028
summary: U.S. chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) announced a significant investment of $400 million in India over the next five years, including the establishment of its largest design center in Bengaluru, creating 3,000 new engineering jobs. This move aligns with India's efforts to become a chipmaking hub, attracting other major players like Applied Materials and Micron with its incentive programs. AMD's expansion underscores the country's growing importance in the global semiconductor industry.

title: UMC forecasts utilization rate to fall to 65%
summary: United Microelectronics Corp (UMC) anticipates its factory utilization rate will drop further to about 65% in the current quarter due to prolonged inventory correction and weak end-market demand. This represents the lowest utilization since Q4 2011, and the company finds it difficult to predict a bottom given customer inventory destocking through next quarter. Despite this, UMC plans to expand its 28-nanometer capacity and is doubling its silicon interposer wafer capacity to meet growing demand for AI chips.

title: Micron Delivers Industry's Fastest, Highest-Capacity HBM to Advance Generative AI Innovation
summary: Micron Technology announced it has begun sampling the industry's first 8-high 24 GB HBM3 Gen2 memory, boasting bandwidth greater than 1.2 TB/s and pin speed over 9.2 Gb/s, a significant improvement over existing HBM3 solutions. This new memory offers a 2.5 times performance per watt improvement, setting new benchmarks for AI data center metrics and reducing training times for large language models like GPT-4. Micron's 12-high stack with 36 GB capacity is expected to sample in early 2024, further enhancing capacity and efficiency for generative AI and HPC applications.

title: Nvidia is ‘dominating’ and could unlock $300 billion in AI revenue by 2027, analyst says
summary: Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh is increasingly optimistic about Nvidia's prospects, projecting the company could tap into $300 billion in AI-related revenue by 2027. Rakesh believes Nvidia will maintain a significant share in the AI server market despite potential future competition. This outlook comes as Nvidia's stock has already seen a 200% increase this year.

title: Microsoft and Meta expand their AI partnership with Llama 2 on Azure and Windows
summary: Microsoft and Meta are expanding their AI partnership, bringing Meta's Llama 2 large language models to Azure and Windows. This collaboration aims to democratize AI by providing developers with open models, enabling them to build generative AI tools and experiences. Azure customers can now fine-tune and deploy Llama 2 models, while Windows developers can run Llama locally, integrating AI safety features from both companies.

title: Aehr Reports Record Revenue and Profit for Fiscal 2023 and Guides for Over 50% Increase in Revenue for Fiscal 2024 on Strength from Semiconductor Wafer Level Test and Burn-in Demand
summary: Aehr Test Systems announced record financial results for fiscal 2023, with net sales reaching $65.0 million and GAAP net income of $14.6 million, driven by demand for semiconductor wafer level test and burn-in products. The company also provided strong guidance for fiscal 2024, projecting revenue of at least $100 million, a 50% increase, and GAAP net income of at least $28 million, reflecting over 90% growth. This growth is attributed to increased adoption of their FOX systems and WaferPak Contactors for silicon carbide in electric vehicles, as well as new opportunities in silicon photonics and gallium nitride markets.

title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. – More market share gains expected
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is expected to gain further market share in the data center CPU market and capitalize on opportunities to expand its presence in the data center GPU market due to increased generative AI adoption. The company's margins are projected to grow post-acquisition of Xilinx and Pensando, driven by increasing revenue contributions from its Data Centre and Embedded segments. Phillip Securities Research initiates coverage with an Accumulate recommendation and a target price of US$125.00, anticipating marginal revenue growth in FY23e and re-acceleration in FY24e.

title: Chipmaker Micron beats on demand from booming AI, easing glut
summary: Micron Technology exceeded third-quarter revenue estimates driven by high demand for its memory chips in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence sector and an easing supply glut in traditional markets. The company's shares rose over 2% after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and anticipating improved pricing trends. Despite ongoing U.S.-China tech tensions impacting its presence in the Chinese market, Micron expressed confidence in the memory industry's recovery.

title: Nvidia and AMD shares fall on report of new U.S. ban on AI chip exports to China
summary: Shares of Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. dropped following a report that the Biden administration is considering a new ban on sales of AI chips to China. This potential ban comes despite Nvidia managing to avoid $400 million in lost sales last year after a previous ban on some chip sales to China. The news impacted both companies with Nvidia shares falling 3% after hours and AMD shares also decreasing by 3%.

title: The A.I. Race Is Now Between Two Chip Giants Led by Taiwanese American CEOs
summary: The generative A.I. boom has intensified competition between semiconductor giants Nvidia and AMD, who are racing to produce advanced A.I. chips. AMD recently announced the MI300X, a direct competitor to Nvidia's H100, aiming to challenge Nvidia's dominant market share in the A.I. chip sector. Both companies are led by Taiwanese American CEOs, Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Lisa Su of AMD, who share similar backgrounds and have played pivotal roles in their companies' success in the semiconductor industry.

title: AMD is chasing down Nvidia in AI, but one analyst worries the company is ‘somewhat late’
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) is pursuing the lucrative AI data-center market, estimated to be worth $150 billion, following recent product announcements. While many analysts praised AMD's efforts, Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon expressed concerns that AMD is "somewhat late" to the AI race compared to rival Nvidia Corp. Rasgon noted that AMD's AI discussion offered limited "hard numbers" and a timeline that seemed delayed relative to the competition.

title: AMD launches new Instinct MI300X AI chip to take on Nvidia’s GPUs
summary: AMD has launched its new Instinct MI300X AI accelerator chip, designed to compete with Nvidia's GPUs in the generative AI market. The company also introduced its Infinity Architecture Platform, powered by eight MI300X chips, and its ROCm software ecosystem. Despite these announcements, AMD's stock fell due to a lack of major customer endorsements for the new chips and details on pricing.

title: AMD launches new data-center AI chips, software to go up against Nvidia and Intel
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) unveiled new data-center AI chips and software, including the Instinct MI300X accelerator and MI300A, to compete with Nvidia Corp. and Intel Corp. Despite these announcements at its Data Center & AI Technology Premiere event, AMD's stock declined, finishing down 3.6%. The new products are specifically aimed at handling generative-AI workloads.

title: NVIDIA Announces DGX GH200 AI Supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the DGX GH200 AI supercomputer, designed to handle massive models for generative AI, recommender systems, and data analytics. This new system connects 256 Grace Hopper Superchips to function as a single 1-exaflop, 144TB GPU, offering significantly more memory than its predecessor. Companies like Google Cloud, Meta, and Microsoft are among the first to explore its capabilities, and NVIDIA is also building its own Helios supercomputer based on this design.

title: Nvidia stock price is surging thanks to ChatGPT and an expected boom in generative AI
summary: Nvidia's stock price surged over 26% after forecasting Q2 2024 revenue of $11 billion, significantly above Wall Street estimates, due to the increasing demand for its powerful GPU chips needed for generative AI technologies like ChatGPT. Despite a slight decrease in Q1 2024 revenue compared to the previous year, the company's strong future outlook based on the generative AI boom is driving investor confidence, also positively impacting other chipmakers like AMD. Nvidia's CEO stated that the company is greatly increasing its supply to meet the surging demand for its data center products.

title: SOXQ Top Holdings List & Exposure (Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings and exposure for the Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXQ). It breaks down the fund's investments by company, geographic region, currency, sector, and industry. The top holdings include NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Advanced Micro Devices, with a significant allocation to the United States and the technology sector, specifically semiconductors.

title: Applied Materials plans to build US$4bn R&D center
summary: Applied Materials plans to invest up to US$4 billion to construct a new Research and Development (R&D) center in Silicon Valley, aiming to accelerate semiconductor manufacturing innovation. This "EPIC Center" would be the largest R&D facility in the semiconductor industry and is envisioned to speed up the transition of academic research to factory production, while also potentially leveraging funding from the US CHIPS and Science Act. The project seeks to address technical challenges and attract talent crucial for the industry's growth.

title: Supermicro Launches Industry's First NVIDIA HGX H100 8 and 4-GPU H100 Servers with Liquid Cooling -- Reduces Data Center Power Costs by Up to 40%
summary: Supermicro has introduced the industry's first NVIDIA HGX H100 8 and 4-GPU servers featuring liquid cooling, designed to significantly reduce data center power costs by up to 40%. These new rack-scale solutions accelerate deployment, enhance performance, and lower operating expenses, also offering an estimated 86% reduction in direct cooling costs compared to air-cooled data centers. The servers support high-performance AI workloads with NVIDIA HGX H100 Tensor Core GPUs and are integrated with advanced liquid cooling systems to optimize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and Total Cost to Environment (TCE).

title: Applied Materials plans $4B Silicon Valley R&D facility
summary: Applied Materials announced plans to invest up to $4 billion in a new Silicon Valley research and development facility. This "EPIC Center" will focus on advancing semiconductor manufacturing and is expected to house over $25 billion in research work within its first decade. The investment is contingent on receiving funding from the CHIPS and Science Act, aiming to accelerate the industry's ability to bring new technologies to market.

title: Supermicro Launches Industry's First NVIDIA HGX H100 8 and 4-GPU H100 Servers with Liquid Cooling -- Reduces Data Center Power Costs by Up to 40%
summary: Supermicro has launched the industry's first NVIDIA HGX H100 8 and 4-GPU servers featuring liquid cooling, designed to significantly reduce data center power costs by up to 40%. These new rack-scale solutions accelerate deployment and increase performance for AI and HPC workloads, while also lowering operating expenses and improving Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) by up to 86% in direct cooling costs. The systems offer up to 30x performance improvement over previous generations for large transformer models and boast advanced features like PCIe 5.0 and NVIDA H100 SXM5 Tensor Core GPUs.

title: Growing chip supply helps Baxter slash backlog
summary: Baxter International significantly reduced its backlog for Front Line Care products by half in Q1, thanks to an improved supply of electromechanical components, including semiconductor chips. This improved availability has allowed the healthcare company to reduce spot purchasing, lower costs, and enhance operational predictability, though an elevated backlog still remains which the company aims to address throughout the year. Despite facing continued pressure from rising supply chain costs from suppliers, Baxter expresses cautious optimism about turning the corner on component supply.

title: Semiconductor Stocks Are Hot -- So Is Their Long-Term Outlook
summary: Semiconductor stocks and related ETFs, like the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), have experienced significant growth this year, driven largely by enthusiasm for artificial intelligence, particularly due to companies like Nvidia. While concerns about valuation exist, analysts believe the long-term outlook remains attractive, bolstered by a rebounding PC and smartphone market, and the massive potential of AI development across industries.

title: Stock of the week - Advanced Micro Devices (29.06.2023)
summary: This article discusses the potential impact of new US chip export restrictions to China on Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). While such restrictions negatively affected semiconductor stocks, AMD's exposure may be limited as China's share of its revenue has significantly decreased. The article also compares AMD's stock performance to Nvidia and Intel, noting Nvidia's stronger recovery from the 2022 sell-off.

title: Oracle is no longer buying Intel processors for its data centers
summary: Oracle, one of the largest data center operators globally, has stopped purchasing Intel processors for its data centers. This decision was confirmed by Oracle Chairman Larry Ellison. Instead of Intel, Oracle is now buying billions of dollars worth of Nvidia and AMD chips.

title: Artificial Intelligence Opens a Generational Opportunity for Chipmakers
summary: The article discusses how the expansion of AI applications, especially large language models, is creating a "generational opportunity" for chipmakers. It highlights the projected growth of AI chip spending to nearly $165 billion by the end of the decade, primarily benefiting GPU-based chip providers like Nvidia, and notes that the demand for specialized AI hardware is leading to significant investments, partnerships, and a potential "long capital investment cycle" for the semiconductor industry. The article also examines how this shift will impact traditional CPU providers and accelerate the replacement of legacy computing infrastructure with AI-first hardware.

title: Spear Alpha ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (SPRX)
summary: The Spear Alpha ETF (SPRX) currently holds an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" based on 557 analyst ratings covering 25 companies within its portfolio. These companies represent 99.4% of the ETF's holdings. The aggregate price target for SPRX is $37.53, with individual holdings showing possible upsides ranging from -26.1% to 75.3%.

title: Fidelity Metaverse ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (FMET)
summary: The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" with an average price target equal to its current share price of $36.66. The rating is based on 613 analyst ratings covering 20 companies (69.5% of the portfolio) over the past year. The ETF's top holdings include major tech companies like AMD, Alphabet, Apple, and NVIDIA.

title: AMD's AI chip challenge to Nvidia remains uphill fight with no big customers named
summary: AMD unveiled new details about its MI300X artificial intelligence chip, designed to challenge Nvidia's market dominance, but did not announce any major customers for the product. While the chip offers significant memory capacity aimed at cost reduction for AI services, the lack of customer commitments disappointed Wall Street, causing AMD's stock to fall. Analysts noted that Nvidia's strong market position is reinforced by its software ecosystem, which AMD is attempting to counter with its Rocm platform.

title: Applied Materials Announces $4 Billion Investment In EPIC Center For R&D Collaboration
summary: Applied Materials is investing $4 billion into its new Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a collaborative R&D project designed to accelerate semiconductor production techniques. This initiative aims to reduce the time from foundational research to mass commercialization by 30% through overlapping R&D phases and fostering direct collaboration between universities, equipment makers, and chip companies. The EPIC Center will strengthen Applied Materials' position in the industry, benefit chip makers with faster product roadmaps, and provide invaluable learning opportunities for university students.

title: Intel's Arc A750 graphics card is only $200 at Newegg
summary: Intel's Arc A750 graphics card is currently available for $200 on Newegg, a $50 discount, making it an excellent option for affordable 1080p gaming. This deal is significant as GPU prices are decreasing due to increased competition from Intel's Arc series. The card performs best with motherboards supporting Resizeable BAR, especially for DirectX 12 titles.

title: Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:SOXQ)
summary: The Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXQ) tracks a market-cap-weighted index of 30 U.S.-listed semiconductor companies, launched in June 2021. As of March 2026, SOXQ was trading at $64.09, showing a 14.9% increase year-to-date, with key holdings including NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Advanced Micro Devices. The ETF manages over $1 billion in assets, driven partly by significant investments in AI chip stocks.

title: ASE, Amkor, UMC and Samsung Getting a Slice of the CoWoS Market from AI Chips, Challenging TSMC
summary: The surging demand for AI chips is overwhelming TSMC's CoWoS packaging capacity, leading chipmakers like Nvidia to diversify their supply chains. This shift creates opportunities for other foundries and OSATs such as UMC, ASE (including SPIL), and Samsung, which are developing their own advanced packaging solutions to meet the growing market needs. Samsung, with its turnkey service and significant R&D investments in 2.5D packaging, is actively pursuing a larger share of the AI chip market.

title: Implications and Updates From China’s National People’s Conference
summary: China's annual "Two Sessions" parliamentary meeting revealed strategic policies for economic growth, trade, and technology, targeting a 5% GDP growth in 2023 driven by domestic consumption. The conference highlighted key implications for sectors like EVs, clean energy, cloud computing, biotechnology, and semiconductors, emphasizing self-reliance and technological innovation. Government restructuring and increased focus on digital infrastructure and R&D are expected to significantly impact various industries and investment themes in China.

title: AMD to Make 'New' 2019-Era 3000G APUs to Sell Old Motherboards
summary: AMD is reportedly resuming production of its 2019-era 12nm Zen+ Ryzen 3000G APUs, specifically the Ryzen 3 3200G and Ryzen 5 3400G, with plans to produce 30,000 new chips. This move is believed to be an effort to stimulate sales of older AM4 motherboards, particularly in the Chinese market. The article notes that price adjustments will be necessary for these dated APUs to be competitive against newer, similarly priced options like the Ryzen 5 5600G.

title: Samsung primed for graphics chip leadership with GDDR7
summary: Samsung Electronics has unveiled the industry's first GDDR7 DRAM, which is faster and more energy-efficient than existing models. This new graphics memory product boasts a data transfer speed of 32 Gbps, making it able to process 50 ultra-high definition movies in one second, and consumes 20% less power than its predecessor. Samsung expects this technology to elevate user experiences in areas requiring outstanding graphics performance like AI, high-performance computing, and autonomous vehicles, positioning them to lead the graphics chip market.

title: Nvidia’s stock could have a pathway to $600, Citi says
summary: Citi Research analyst Atif Malik has raised his price target for Nvidia Corp. stock to $520 from $420, citing the company's dominance in the rapidly growing artificial intelligence accelerator market. Malik also outlined a bull-case scenario where Nvidia's stock could reach $600. He anticipates blistering growth in the AI accelerator market, with Nvidia poised to outperform competitors.

title: Intel Reveals Fastest Arc Pro Workstation GPUs Yet
summary: Intel has launched its fastest Arc Pro workstation GPUs to date, the A60 for desktops and A60M for laptops, significantly increasing specifications over previous models. These new GPUs are designed for applications like CAD, AI inferencing, and media processing, aiming to challenge the market dominance of Nvidia and AMD. While Intel hopes to attract workstation users with improved performance and quarterly driver updates, some partners note a lack of demand and suggest Intel needs a more comprehensive solution to compete effectively.

title: Notable Wins
summary: The I/O Fund has achieved significant returns since its inception, outperforming major indices with a cumulative return of 326%. In 2025 alone, the fund returned 37%, positioning it as a top-performing hedge fund. The article details specific successful investments in companies like Bloom Energy, Astera Labs, Nvidia, and various cryptocurrencies, highlighting the fund's strategic allocation to AI and early insights into market trends.

title: The Cheap Trick Alphabet Is Using To Boost Its Share Price
summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by Apple and Tesla, is unlikely to fundamentally change the company's valuation but aims to make shares more accessible to smaller investors and potentially gain entry into the Dow Jones Industrial Average. While some tech giants saw significant share price boosts post-split, Alphabet's future success might be tempered by changing market conditions. The article suggests Amazon could be the next tech giant to undertake a similar split to boost its stock.

title: AMD Q1 Earnings Preview: Analysts Bullish, But Warn Of Factors That 'Can Derail The Semiconductor Industry'
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) is set to release its Q1 earnings, with analysts expecting revenue of $5.46 billion and earnings of 61 cents per share. While many analysts are bullish due to strong AI MI300 and EPYC performance, they also highlight risks such as market share declines, intense competition, and macroeconomic uncertainties that could impact the semiconductor industry. AMD shares have performed well over the last year, but some analysts have adjusted price targets ahead of the report.

title: 2024 Beijing Auto Show: WeRide's four major products officially debut.
summary: WeRide, a leader in autonomous driving technology, unveiled four core products at the 2024 Beijing Auto Show, including a L2++ mass-produced car, Robotaxi, Robobus, and an autonomous road sweeper. The company showcased these products and offered test rides, highlighting its advanced development capabilities and contributions to the intelligent driving industry. WeRide also emphasized its collaboration with Bosch and the commercial operation success of its autonomous taxi and minibus in various cities.

title: UMC reports lowest profit in three years
summary: United Microelectronic Corp (UMC) reported its lowest net profit in nearly three years in the first quarter, at NT$10.46 billion, due to prolonged inventory correction. However, the company anticipates a 3 percent increase in wafer shipments for the current quarter, driven by improving demand in communication and computer devices. UMC maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook for the year, expecting to outperform the global foundry industry and forecasting global semiconductor industry growth of about 5 percent, largely led by AI servers.

title: Nvidia acquires GPU cluster optimization startup Run:ai for reported $700M
summary: Nvidia Corp. has acquired Run:ai, a startup specializing in software that optimizes the performance of graphics card clusters for AI workloads. Although the terms were not officially disclosed, the deal was reportedly valued at $700 million, significantly higher than Run:ai's prior funding. Run:ai's technology aims to boost AI performance by resolving common inefficiencies in GPU-powered servers, such as data exchange delays and memory collisions, allowing for more efficient utilization of GPU resources.

title: US chip giant Nvidia snaps up Israeli AI workload management startup
summary: Nvidia has acquired Run:ai, an Israeli startup specializing in AI workload management software, for an estimated $600-$700 million. This acquisition marks Nvidia's largest in Israel since its 2020 purchase of Mellanox Technologies. Run:ai's co-founders and employees will join Nvidia's expanding R&D operations in Israel, aiming to enhance the efficiency of AI computing resources for customers across various infrastructure environments.

title: NVIDIA to Acquire GPU Orchestration Software Provider Run:ai
summary: NVIDIA announced its definitive agreement to acquire Run:ai, a Kubernetes-based workload management and orchestration software provider. This acquisition aims to help customers optimize their AI computing resources across various environments, with NVIDIA continuing to invest in Run:ai's product roadmap and integrate its capabilities with NVIDIA's AI platforms. The acquisition will enable better GPU utilization and improved management for customers leveraging NVIDIA's accelerated computing platform.

title: Serve Robotics Hauls In $40M and Prepares to Put 2,000 Robots on Streets
summary: Serve Robotics has raised $40 million, bringing its total fundraising to $93 million since 2021, and plans to deploy 2,000 robots in new markets by the end of 2025. The company aims to expand operations in Los Angeles and enter new cities like Dallas, San Diego, and Vancouver, having formalized a partnership with Magna International for manufacturing. Serve highlights safety, labor savings, and adorability as key value propositions, with CEO Dr. Ali Kashani expressing confidence in scalability despite being in early pre-revenue stages.

title: Cadence emulator and prototyping duo can handle up to 48 billion gate SoCs
summary: Cadence Design Systems has introduced its third-generation Palladium Z3 emulation and Protium X3 FPGA prototyping systems, offering significant capacity and performance improvements for advanced SoC development. These systems can handle designs from 16 million up to 48 billion gates, enabling comprehensive testing of large SoCs. Powered by Nvidia's BlueField DPU and Quantum InfiniBand, the solutions are designed to accelerate hardware verification and software validation, especially for AI, automotive, and hyperscale applications.

title: Microsoft CEO to meet with Samsung, SK Hynix, LG, SK Telecom chiefs
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and founder Bill Gates will meet with leaders of Samsung, SK Hynix, LG, and SK Telecom at the MS CEO Summit 2024 in May to discuss strengthening AI partnerships. The meetings aim to explore joint development of AI chips, cooperation in AI technology for consumer electronics, and business tie-ups in 5G telecommunications and cloud sectors. This gathering signifies an increasing trend of Big Tech firms seeking AI business collaborations to gain a competitive edge.

title: Akamai Launches Cloud Infrastructure and Services Powered by NVIDIA for Enhanced Video Processing
summary: Akamai Technologies has launched a new media-optimized cloud offering leveraging NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation GPUs to enhance video processing for the media and entertainment industry. This service aims to provide significantly faster encoding and transcoding compared to traditional CPU-based methods, offering scalable and reliable architectures for various demanding workflows. Beyond media, the GPUs are also applicable to generative AI/ML, data analysis, scientific computing, gaming, and high-performance computing.

title: Super Micro Computer stock crashes 23%, drags down AI darling Nvidia after it doesn't preannounce earnings
summary: Super Micro Computer stock plunged 23% after the company announced its Q3 earnings date without a preannouncement, unlike last year. This lack of a positive preannouncement sparked investor concerns about the strength of its upcoming results. The decline also impacted Nvidia, whose chips are used in Super Micro's servers, causing its stock to fall by about 10%.

title: TSMC Accelerates Nearshoring to Diversify Away from China
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is significantly expanding its manufacturing presence in the United States, increasing its investment from $40 billion to $65 billion, primarily in Phoenix, Arizona. This strategic move, supported by $6.6 billion in U.S. government subsidies, aims to decentralize chip production away from Taiwan, enhance U.S. technological sovereignty, and create thousands of jobs. The expansion reflects a broader industry trend towards nearshoring and diversifying supply chains to mitigate geopolitical risks and reduce reliance on Asian markets for advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

title: Cisco Reimagines Security for Data Centers and Clouds in Era of AI
summary: Cisco has unveiled Hypershield, a new security architecture designed to protect data centers and clouds in the era of AI. This innovation allows for security placement anywhere it's needed, providing AI-native security capabilities such as autonomous network segmentation and distributed exploit protection. Cisco Hypershield aims to tip the scales in favor of defenders against sophisticated AI-driven cyber threats, leveraging hardware acceleration and cloud-native technologies like eBPF.

title: 4 Undervalued Semiconductor Stocks
summary: Amidst the AI boom led by Nvidia, Morningstar analysts identify Infineon Technologies, STMicroelectronics, MediaTek, and Skyworks Solutions as undervalued semiconductor stocks. The article discusses the varying valuations between digital and analog chipmakers, highlighting the robust demand for AI-related semiconductors versus the mixed recovery in non-AI sectors like automotive, industrial, and personal electronics. It provides detailed reasons for each company's valuation and market position.

title: SiTime Continues to Advance Precision Timing with an Integrated Clock Chip for AI Datacenters
summary: SiTime Corporation introduced its Chorus™ family of clock generators designed for AI datacenter applications. This new MEMS-based clock-system-on-a-chip (ClkSoC) family offers 10X higher performance in half the size compared to traditional standalone oscillators and clocks, integrating all necessary timing components into a single chip. The solution aims to simplify system architecture, accelerate design time, and address issues like noise and impedance matching, providing significant benefits for datacenter equipment.

title: Cadence Supercharges Chip Debug And Prototyping With Palladium Z3 And Protium X3 Systems
summary: Cadence Design Systems has launched its new Palladium Z3 and Protium X3 systems, designed to significantly enhance chip debugging and advanced prototyping. The Palladium Z3 offers 1.5 times the performance and double the capacity of its predecessor for pre-silicon debugging, while the Protium X3, built with AMD Versal Premium VP1902 adaptive SoCs, provides 1.5 times faster performance and triple the capacity for advanced physical prototyping. These systems are crucial for accelerating the development of complex chips in the AI era, with general availability expected in Q3 2024.

title: Intel Builds World’s Largest Neuromorphic System to Enable More Sustainable AI
summary: Intel has developed Hala Point, the world's largest neuromorphic system, featuring 1.15 billion neurons and 1,152 Loihi 2 processors to address the efficiency and sustainability challenges of AI. Deployed at Sandia National Laboratories, this system aims to advance brain-inspired AI research and future real-time continuous learning for various applications. It achieves state-of-the-art computational efficiencies, rivaling and exceeding GPU and CPU architectures, and promises significant energy savings for future AI deployments.

title: AMD and Nvidia unveil new processors for AI PCs
summary: AMD and Nvidia have both launched new processors designed for AI PCs, aiming to capitalize on the growing market for computers capable of running AI workloads on-device. AMD introduced its Ryzen PRO 8040 and 8000 Series processors, emphasizing their AI-enabled features for business users, while Nvidia unveiled new RTX A400 and A1000 GPUs with enhanced Tensor and RT Cores for accelerating AI and graphics tasks. This move by both companies highlights the intensifying competition in the AI PC sector, which analysts predict will drive new growth in the overall PC market.

title: Like Nvidia Stock but Prefer ETFs? This Is the Best Semiconductor ETF to Invest In Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Other Megatrends.
summary: The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is highlighted as an excellent option for investors seeking exposure to the semiconductor industry and megatrends like AI, vehicle electrification, and autonomous driving, while mitigating the risk of investing in individual stocks like Nvidia (NVDA). The ETF has Nvidia as its largest holding, accounting for 20% of its portfolio, and has significantly outperformed the S&P 500 over various timeframes due to its focus on the robustly growing chip market. It provides diversification across the semiconductor value chain, including chip producers, foundries, and equipment manufacturers.

title: Cohesity completes late-stage $150M funding from IBM and Nvidia, expands IBM partnership
summary: Data management provider Cohesity Inc. has completed a $150 million Series F funding round with participation from IBM and Nvidia Corp., bringing its total raised to $955 million. The funding coincides with an expanded partnership with IBM, focusing on cyber resilience capabilities within hybrid cloud environments. This collaboration integrates Cohesity DataProtect into IBM Storage Defender to enhance data protection, monitoring, management, and recovery against cyberthreats.

title: TSMC Arizona and U.S. Department of Commerce Announce up to US$6.6 Billion in Proposed CHIPS Act Direct Funding, the Company Plans Third Leading-Edge Fab in Phoenix
summary: TSMC Arizona and the U.S. Department of Commerce have signed a preliminary memorandum for up to US$6.6 billion in CHIPS Act direct funding. TSMC plans to build a third advanced semiconductor fab in Phoenix, Arizona, bringing its total investment in the site to over US$65 billion. This expansion aims to enhance U.S. semiconductor manufacturing capabilities and create thousands of high-tech jobs, with production from the three fabs utilizing 4nm, 2nm, and more advanced processes.

title: Alger Concentrated Equity ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Alger Concentrated Equity ETF (CNEQ), which was created on April 5, 2024. The ETF focuses on large-cap companies with high growth potential, maintaining a concentrated portfolio of no more than 30 stocks. The reported holdings include major technology companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon, alongside others across various sectors.

title: Should You Invest in the Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (IGPT)?
summary: The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (IGPT) offers broad exposure to the Technology - Software segment, particularly in AI and next-gen software development. Launched in 2005, it is passively managed with an expense ratio of 0.60% and currently holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 1 (Strong Buy). Its top holdings include Meta Platforms, Nvidia, and Advanced Micro Devices, and it has shown strong year-to-date performance.

title: Leading chipmaker TSMC evacuates staff and pauses some machinery after Taiwan's largest earthquake in a quarter-century
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), the world's largest advanced chipmaker, and its rival United Microelectronics Corp. (UMC) halted some machinery and evacuated staff after Taiwan experienced its strongest earthquake in 25 years. The 7.4 magnitude temblor raised concerns about the semiconductor supply chain's vulnerability, given Taiwan's critical role in producing high-end chips. TSMC shares slid about 1.5% and UMC less than 1% in early trading following the event.

title: Lowe’s looks to Nvidia and AI to improve its retail operations
summary: Lowe's is partnering with Nvidia to integrate AI across its retail operations, including digital businesses, supply chain, and in-store experiences. The collaboration aims to enhance customer interactions, empower associates, and optimize store management through technologies such as AI-powered visualizations, digital twins in Nvidia Omniverse, and computer vision for checkout efficiency. Lowe's has been leveraging AI for years and sees ripe applications for the technology in improving both business processes and customer satisfaction.

title: 5 Best Momentum ETFs To Buy

summary: NXP Semiconductors has announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to enable the deployment of NVIDIA's trained AI models on NXP's edge processing devices through the eIQ machine learning development environment. summary: Nvidia has unveiled its new Blackwell GPU architecture, designed to power trillion-parameter generative AI models with significantly reduced cost and power consumption compared to previous generations. title: Nvidia and Johnson & Johnson to develop new AI applications for surgery
summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech is collaborating with Nvidia to develop and scale new artificial intelligence applications for surgery. summary: Johnson & Johnson MedTech is collaborating with NVIDIA to integrate advanced AI capabilities into its digital ecosystem for surgery. summary: NVIDIA has announced Project GR00T, a general-purpose foundation model for humanoid robots, along with significant updates to its Isaac robotics platform. title: NVIDIA Blackwell Platform Arrives to Power a New Era of Computing
summary: NVIDIA has announced the Blackwell platform, a new GPU architecture designed to power the next generation of AI and accelerated computing. summary: NVIDIA announced that TSMC and Synopsys are using NVIDIA's cuLitho computational lithography platform in production to accelerate semiconductor manufacturing and enable new generative AI algorithms. summary: NVIDIA announced that major transportation companies are adopting its DRIVE Thor centralized car computer for next-generation consumer and commercial vehicles, including EVs, trucks, and robotaxis. summary: NetApp has announced new leading AFF A-Series systems designed for unified data storage in the AI era, capable of handling demanding IT workloads including GenAI and VMware.
