summary: Concerns about an AI bubble akin to the dot-com bust are overblown, according to J.P. Morgan Private Bank, citing lower valuations and stronger earnings expectations for current AI leaders. While investing in an S&P 500 index fund provides some AI exposure, investors seeking outperformance should diversify across AI infrastructure (AI 1.0) and AI applications (AI 2.0), potentially including global companies and low-cost ETFs for broader exposure. A long-term perspective is crucial as AI is expected to be a multi-year or multi-decade trend.

title: ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood’s tech bargain hunt
summary: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest continued its strategy of investing in tech stocks in September 2022, acquiring shares in companies like Nvidia and Adobe despite significant market downturns for these firms. The ARK Innovation ETF has seen substantial losses and outflows, but the firm is betting on a rebound in battered tech stocks. Additionally, there has been a management reshuffle within ARK Invest, with William Scherer taking over two ETFs and Brett Winton promoted to chief futurist.

title: How Arm conquered the chip market without making a single chip, with CEO Rene Haas
summary: In this interview, Arm CEO Rene Haas discusses how Arm has become a central player in the tech ecosystem by designing chip instruction sets without manufacturing chips themselves. He explains Arm's licensing and royalty business model, its broad customer base including giants like Apple and Qualcomm, and how it is diversifying into cloud, automotive, and IoT markets. Haas also addresses the company's decision to go public, its role in navigating the chip shortage, and its competitive stance against x86 and RISC-V architectures.

title: Chipmaker Qualcomm says automotive future business expands to $30 bln
summary: Qualcomm announced its automotive business pipeline has grown to $30 billion, an increase of over $10 billion since July, attributed to its Snapdragon Digital Chassis product. The company projects significant revenue growth in its automotive segment, from an estimated $1.3 billion in fiscal year 2022 to over $9 billion by fiscal year 2031, and aims for a total addressable market of $100 billion by 2030. Qualcomm also expanded its partnership with Mercedes Benz for in-car infotainment systems and addressed concerns about U.S. export regulations impacting its business in China.

title: Supermicro Delivers Second-Generation NVIDIA® OVX™ Computing System for 3D Collaboration, Metaverse, and Digital Twin Simulation, Powered by the New NVIDIA L40 GPU
summary: Supermicro has launched its second-generation NVIDIA OVX computing systems, powered by the new NVIDIA L40 GPU, designed to accelerate 3D collaboration, metaverse applications, and digital twin simulations. These servers are optimized for NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise applications, offering advanced graphics, AI, and networking performance. The systems support up to eight NVIDIA L40 GPUs, ConnectX-7 SmartNICs, high-performance CPUs, and NVMe storage.

title: Supermicro Delivers Second-Generation NVIDIA® OVX™ Computing System for 3D Collaboration, Metaverse, and Digital Twin Simulation, Powered by the New NVIDIA L40 GPU
summary: Supermicro announced the release of its second-generation NVIDIA OVX computing system, powered by the new NVIDIA L40 GPU, designed for 3D collaboration, metaverse, and digital twin simulation. These new servers aim to provide the necessary graphics, AI, and network performance for building and operating immersive 3D virtual worlds at data center scale. The systems will support up to eight NVIDIA L40 GPUs, ConnectX-7 SmartNICs, and current/future CPU processors from Intel and AMD.

title: ‘Moore’s Law’s dead,’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says in justifying gaming-card price hike
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that "Moore's Law is dead" as he defended the price hike for the company's next-generation gaming cards, Ada Lovelace. He explained that silicon wafers are significantly more expensive to produce. Despite a softening in consumer demand, Huang anticipates a strong Q4 for Ada, citing high demand for their new chips.

title: Shaping Kroger’s Self-Checkout of Tomorrow with AI and Edge Computing
summary: Kroger is enhancing its self-checkout experience and reducing stock losses by implementing Everseen’s Visual AI platform, powered by Lenovo’s AI retail solutions and NVIDIA Accelerated Computing AI Platform. This technology utilizes Edge AI servers and high-resolution cameras to detect and correct scanning errors, providing real-time insights and improving inventory management. The solution has been successfully piloted and is being rolled out across Kroger's stores, significantly reducing retail shrink and improving customer experience without extensive associate intervention.

title: Kodiak Robotics relies on lightweight mapping for autonomous truck PNT
summary: Kodiak Robotics is developing autonomous truck technology for long-haul routes, focusing on a "lightweight mapping" approach that prioritizes reliability over high-definition mapping. The company has announced partnerships with Pilot Company and others to expand its service footprint, integrate its fourth-generation autonomous truck technology, and address the critical need for robust PNT solutions. Kodiak aims to integrate its self-driving software and hardware into production customer trucks by early 2025.

title: Nvidia CEO sees 'large space' for China sales despite U.S. restrictions
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that he still sees a large market for Nvidia's data center chips in China, despite U.S. export restrictions on two of its top chips (A100 and H100). Huang noted that the restrictions have specific performance thresholds that leave a "large space" for Nvidia's other products in the Chinese market, as the majority of their customers are not affected. He also indicated that Nvidia would seek licenses from the U.S. government for Chinese customers desiring the restricted high-end chips.

title: Nvidia’s new AI-focused chip produces more realistic images in games
summary: Nvidia Corp. has unveiled its new AI-focused graphics chip, the RTX 4090, which is designed to produce more realistic images in games by combining AI with traditional pixel calculations. The high-end chip, costing US$1,599, features 76 billion transistors and 24GB of memory, and will go on sale October 12, with other versions following in November. This launch aims to give customers a reason to upgrade amidst a slowdown in PC component demand.

title: Logitech G Elevates Game Streaming By Unveiling Cloud First Handheld Gaming Device
summary: Logitech G has launched the G CLOUD Gaming Handheld, a dedicated cloud gaming device developed in partnership with Tencent Games. This device is optimized for cloud streaming from Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and NVIDIA GeForce NOW, offering precision controls, a 1080p HD screen, and over 12 hours of battery life. It will be available in North America in October 2022 for a suggested retail price of $349.99, with a limited-time pre-order price of $299.99.

title: NVIDIA Unveils DRIVE Thor — Centralized Car Computer Unifying Cluster, Infotainment, Automated Driving, and Parking in a Single, Cost-Saving System
summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Thor, its next-generation centralized computer for autonomous vehicles, delivering up to 2,000 teraflops of performance. This superchip unifies intelligent functions like automated driving, parking, and infotainment into a single architecture, significantly reducing system cost and complexity. ZEEKR, a Geely-owned automaker, is the first customer, planning to integrate DRIVE Thor into its intelligent electric vehicles starting in early 2025.

title: NVIDIA Delivers Quantum Leap in Performance, Introduces New Era of Neural Rendering With GeForce RTX 40 Series
summary: NVIDIA unveiled its new GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs, powered by the Ada Lovelace architecture and new DLSS 3 technology, promising up to 4x performance improvement for gamers and creators. The flagship RTX 4090 and two configurations of the RTX 4080 were introduced, alongside new features like neural rendering and RTX Remix for classic games. These advancements aim to redefine real-time ray tracing, AI-powered graphics, and creative workflows.

title: No Hang Ups With Hangul: KT Trains Smart Speakers, Customer Call Centers With NVIDIA AI
summary: South Korea's leading mobile operator, KT, is leveraging NVIDIA AI to enhance its smart speaker, GiGA Genie, and its AI Contact Center (AICC). By building billion-parameter large language models trained with the NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD platform and NeMo framework, KT has significantly improved language understanding and conversational skills in the complex Korean language, as well as reduced consultation times in their customer service platform. This advancement allows GiGA Genie to offer more human-like interactions and AICC to efficiently manage over 100,000 calls daily.

title: Supermicro Expands Its NVIDIA-Certified Server Portfolio with New NVIDIA H100 Optimized GPU Systems; New Servers Boost AI Training Performance by up to 9x
summary: Supermicro has expanded its NVIDIA-Certified Server portfolio with over 20 new systems optimized for NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering performance gains of up to 9x for AI training. These new servers, available in various form factors, leverage the NVIDIA H100 PCIe and SXM GPUs to accelerate AI/ML, HPC, and inferencing workloads. The systems also include NVIDIA AI Enterprise software for simplified AI development and deployment, promising significant performance improvements and reduced costs for businesses.

title: NVIDIA DRIVE Thor Strikes AI Performance Balance, Uniting AV and Cockpit on a Single Computer
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled DRIVE Thor, a new automotive-grade system-on-a-chip (SoC) designed for autonomous vehicles, targeting 2025 models. This SoC provides 1,000 teraflops of performance and consolidates various vehicle functions like digital cluster, infotainment, and assisted driving onto a single AI computer. DRIVE Thor also incorporates a transformer engine for improved deep neural network accuracy and supports multi-domain computing for efficient task partitioning.

title: NVIDIA Introduces DLSS 3 With Breakthrough AI-Powered Frame Generation for up to 4x Performance
summary: NVIDIA has introduced DLSS 3, an AI-powered performance multiplier that leverages neural rendering to significantly boost frame rates by up to 4x compared to brute-force rendering, while maintaining image quality. This technology, powered by new fourth-generation Tensor Cores and an Optical Flow Accelerator on GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs, generates entire new frames using AI, even benefiting CPU-limited games. Over 35 games and applications, including major titles and game engines like Unity and Unreal Engine, are slated to support DLSS 3.

title: NVIDIA and Booz Allen Hamilton Expand Partnership to Bring AI-Enabled Cybersecurity to Public and Private Sectors
summary: NVIDIA and Booz Allen Hamilton have expanded their partnership to deliver an AI-enabled, GPU-accelerated cybersecurity platform to public and private sector clients. This platform leverages NVIDIA Morpheus and Booz Allen's Cyber Precog to detect and address cybersecurity threats rapidly, even in resource-constrained environments. The collaboration focuses on providing advanced analytical capabilities at the edge, significantly boosting data ingestion, AI training, and inference speeds compared to CPU-only systems.

title: NVIDIA Expands Large Language Models to Biology
summary: NVIDIA has introduced the BioNeMo framework at GTC, which aims to accelerate drug discovery by enabling scientists to train and deploy large biomolecular language models. This framework, part of the NVIDIA Clara Discovery suite, supports various biological data formats like chemistry, protein, DNA, and RNA, helping researchers uncover new insights into biological sequences and their functions. Leading pharmaceutical companies, biotech startups, and research institutions are adopting BioNeMo to create AI applications for generating, predicting, and understanding biomolecular data.

title: HOLO Stock Price and Chart — NASDAQ:HOLO
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of MicroCloud Hologram Inc. (HOLO) stock, including its current price, historical performance, key financial statistics, and company information. It also features a collection of trading ideas and technical analysis indicators for investors interested in HOLO. The company specializes in holographic technology and is headquartered in New York, NY.

title: Direxion Semiconductor (SOXL) Stock Is Down 83%. What’s Next?
summary: The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X Shares (SOXL) ETF has plummeted 83% this year, exhibiting a head and shoulders pattern, which typically signals further losses. Despite this, the ETF has reached a significant support level, potentially setting the stage for a rally. However, investors are cautioned about the risks associated with leveraged ETFs like SOXL, which aim for a 3X daily return of the ICE Semiconductor Index and can amplify both gains and losses.

title: Supermicro Announces 8U H100 HGX Server
summary: Supermicro has announced its new 8U Universal GPU Server, incorporating eight NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, designed for large-scale AI training, NVIDIA Omniverse, and Metaverse applications. This server increases AI performance with improved thermal density, enabling lower power consumption and operation at higher data center temperatures, while supporting both current and next-generation CPUs and GPUs. The company is expanding its leading GPU server lineup with this addition, offering flexibility with front and rear I/O, AC or DC power support, and liquid cooling options.

title: MicroVision's Lidar Solution Supported on NVIDIA DRIVE Autonomous Vehicle Platform
summary: MicroVision announced that its MAVIN DR lidar system is now supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX platform, enabling true highway-pilot functionality for OEMs. This integration aims to accelerate the adoption of advanced safety features in vehicles by providing high-resolution sensor technology with low latency. The MAVIN DR system is also supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE Sim simulation platform for development and validation.

title: Supermicro Adds New 8U Universal GPU Server That Delivers Maximum Performance and Flexibility for Large Scale AI Training, NVIDIA® Omniverse, and Metaverse
summary: Supermicro has launched a new 8U Universal GPU server designed for large-scale AI training, NVIDIA Omniverse, and the Metaverse. This server features eight NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering maximum performance and flexibility. Its advanced airflow design helps reduce Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) in data centers while maintaining high performance.

title: US-China chip war is overheating
summary: The Biden administration plans to expand restrictions on U.S. semiconductor and chipmaking tool exports to China, targeting advanced AI chips and manufacturing equipment. These new regulations will codify earlier limitations imposed on companies like KLA Corp, Lam Research Corp, Applied Materials Inc, Nvidia Corp, and Advanced Micro Devices. The move is part of the U.S. strategy to curb China's technological advancements and strengthen its domestic semiconductor industry through initiatives like the $50 billion CHIPS Act.

title: Nvidia could take a $400M revenue hit from new government restrictions on AI chips
summary: New government restrictions on the sale of AI chips to China could cost Nvidia an estimated $400 million in revenue. Both Nvidia and AMD are facing these limitations on their ability to sell advanced data center chips in the Chinese market.

title: Nvidia says U.S. government allows A.I. chip development in China
summary: Nvidia confirmed that the U.S. government has permitted it to continue developing its H100 artificial intelligence chip in China, despite new export restrictions on high-performance AI chips to the region. The restrictions, which still ban sales of the A100 and H100 chips to China and Russia, are expected to cost Nvidia $400 million in revenue for the current quarter. Developing the H100 in China is allowed, and Nvidia can ship existing AI chips from Hong Kong until September 2023.

title: Nvidia Warns of Sales Hit From New U.S. Chip Licensing Requirements for China
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced that new U.S. licensing requirements for shipping advanced chips to China could result in a loss of up to $400 million in quarterly sales. The company was notified on Friday that it would need a license from the U.S. government for certain cutting-edge chip sales to China and Russia. This development follows President Biden's recent signing of the Chips and Science Act of 2022.

title: Gaming industry advancing development of virtual ecosystem: Co-Founder of Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF
summary: Matthew Ball, CEO and Co-Founder of the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF, discusses the progress of the gaming industry in developing a virtual ecosystem. The discussion covers the future of virtual real estate companies, the capabilities of 3D rendering, and the practical aspects of building a virtual world.

title: AMD launching what it claims is ‘fastest processer in the world for gaming’ in September
summary: AMD announced the launch of its new Ryzen 7000 series gaming processors, touted as the "fastest processor in the world for gaming" by CEO Lisa Su. The processors are based on a 5-nanometer Zen 4 core architecture. This release comes amidst a challenging period for PC sales, with the low-end Ryzen 5 7600x model priced at $299.

title: AMD Set To Become TSMC’s Second Largest 5nm Customer Courtesy Of Ryzen 7000
summary: AMD is projected to become TSMC's second-largest customer for 5nm technology, primarily driven by its upcoming Ryzen 7000 series processors. These new CPUs, including desktop, notebook, and datacenter variants, will extensively utilize TSMC's 5nm process node. This increased demand will solidify AMD's position as a major client for the Taiwanese chip manufacturer, second only to Apple.

title: Nvidia sales forecast falls about $1 billion short of expectations, stock falls
summary: Nvidia's sales forecast for the current quarter fell approximately $1 billion short of analyst expectations, leading to a drop in its stock. The company confirmed a sharp reduction in profit and is working through inventory before releasing its new chip architecture. For the fiscal third quarter, Nvidia predicted revenue between $5.78 billion to $6.02 billion, while analysts had projected $6.91 billion.

title: Intel shares new details about upcoming Meteor Lake processor series
summary: Intel has revealed new technical details about its upcoming Meteor Lake processor series, which will utilize chiplet technology for desktop and laptop CPUs. These processors will feature five chiplets, with the primary CPU module manufactured by Intel and other vital components like the GPU and I/O module produced by TSMC. This chiplet architecture allows for greater flexibility in design, improved manufacturing efficiency, and better performance through 3D stacking with Intel's Foveros technology.

title: Report: Qualcomm plans to return to the server chip market
summary: Qualcomm Inc. is reportedly planning to re-enter the server chip market four years after exiting it, seeking customers for a new server processor. This new processor is based on technology acquired from Nuvia Inc. for $1.4 billion and is being evaluated by Amazon Web Services Inc. The move aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand beyond mobile and boost revenue, potentially increasing competition for Intel Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

title: Lam Research to open its second R&D centre in India
summary: US-based semiconductor equipment supplier Lam Research is establishing its second R&D center in India in September, aiming to enable local design completion and reduce reliance on its US counterparts. The new facility will feature an advanced hardware engineering lab for deposition, etching, and wet processing, alongside AR/VR capabilities. This expansion underscores India's growing importance in the semiconductor design ecosystem, despite the manufacturing sector being in its early stages.

title: AMD Stock Is a Bargain
summary: Morningstar considers AMD stock a bargain with a fair value estimate of $130 per share, giving it a 4-star rating and a narrow economic moat. The company is praised for its impressive growth, market share gains against Intel, and strong execution in new chip designs, especially in the data center and PC markets. However, high uncertainty remains due to the cyclical semiconductor industry and AMD's smaller scale compared to Intel and Nvidia.

title: NVIDIA Announces Major Release of Omniverse With New USD Connectors and Tools, Simulation Technologies and Developer Frameworks
summary: NVIDIA has announced a major update to its Omniverse platform, introducing new developer frameworks, tools, apps, and plugins designed to build and connect metaverse worlds. These enhancements include AI-powered tools like Omniverse Avatar Cloud Engine, DeepSearch, and NeuralVDB, along with 11 new USD Connectors to integrate with leading 3D applications and CAD software. The updates aim to simplify virtual world creation and foster collaboration across industries, bridging the physical and virtual realms.

title: NVIDIA and Partners Build Out Universal Scene Description to Accelerate Industrial Metaverse and Next Wave of AI
summary: NVIDIA, in collaboration with Pixar, Adobe, Autodesk, Siemens, and other industry leaders, is launching a multi-year initiative to expand Universal Scene Description (USD) as a foundational language for the open metaverse and 3D internet. The effort aims to extend USD's capabilities beyond visual effects to support industrial applications like architecture, engineering, manufacturing, robotics, and digital twins, introducing features such as international character support, geospatial coordinates, and real-time IoT data streaming. NVIDIA is also providing open-source resources, a compatibility testing suite, and developing USD plugins for popular 3D software to accelerate its adoption across various industries.

title: Cathie Wood sells Block shares to double down on Nvidia
summary: Ark Invest, led by Cathie Wood, sold over $20 million worth of Block (SQ) shares and simultaneously purchased over $65 million worth of Nvidia (NVDA) shares across three of its funds. This move follows Ark's previous decision to exit PayPal (PYPL) to bet on Block, and comes amidst macroeconomic turbulence causing significant losses in various asset classes, including Block and Bitcoin. Ark also recently sold Coinbase (COIN) shares due to regulatory uncertainty.

title: Nvidia is hit by another ‘crypto hangover,’ and that isn’t the only problem
summary: Nvidia is facing a "crypto hangover" and other issues as the pandemic-era booms in PC sales, videogames, and cryptocurrency decline. The company warned of a $1.4 billion revenue shortfall due to weak gaming equipment sales and excess inventory. Nvidia's stock fell 6.3% on the news, reflecting broader concerns about multiple challenges impacting its core business.

title: Nvidia Warns of Sales Shortfall as Gaming Revenue Drops
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced a significant sales shortfall for the quarter ending July 31, expecting revenue of $6.7 billion, which is 17% below its May forecast. This reduction is primarily due to a 33% drop in gaming revenue, signaling a potential slowdown in the computer chip market after a pandemic-era boom. The company's stock experienced a decline following this announcement.

title: Pelosi’s Taiwan trip puts the world's biggest chipmaker back in the spotlight of U.S.-China rivalry
summary: Nancy Pelosi's visit to Taiwan brought renewed attention to the island's critical role in the global chip supply chain, specifically highlighting Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), a key manufacturer for tech giants like Apple and Nvidia. The visit underscored the strategic importance of semiconductors to U.S. national security and its rivalry with China. TSMC's dominance in the foundry market and the ongoing U.S. efforts to boost domestic chip manufacturing and secure supply chains were central themes, with concerns about China's potential actions towards Taiwan posing a significant risk to the global chip market.

title: UCIe™ (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express™) Consortium Announces Incorporation and New Board Members; Open for Membership
summary: The UCIe™ (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express™) Consortium has officially incorporated and announced new board members, including Alibaba and NVIDIA, joining founding members like ASE, AMD, Intel, and Samsung. The consortium aims to advance the UCIe specification to create a universal and interoperable chiplet ecosystem, with the UCIe 1.0 specification already available for download. They are actively seeking new members to contribute to the development of future specifications.

title: Enabling Enterprise Cybersecurity Protection with a DPU-Accelerated, Next-Generation Firewall
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have collaborated to enhance cybersecurity by accelerating VM-Series Next Generation Firewalls (NGFW) using NVIDIA's BlueField Data Processing Unit (DPU). This partnership provides a 5x performance boost and significant CapEx savings by offloading packet inspection from host CPUs to the DPU. The joint solution includes an Intelligent Traffic Offload (ITO) service that optimizes firewall resources, ensuring deep security inspection only for necessary payload flows, thereby improving efficiency and enabling comprehensive zero-trust protection across all hosts.

title: Pony.ai Express: New Autonomous Trucking Collaboration Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE Orin
summary: Pony.ai and SANY Heavy Truck, China's largest heavy equipment manufacturer, have partnered to develop level 4 autonomous trucks using NVIDIA DRIVE Orin. The collaboration aims to address the rapidly growing package delivery market and driver shortages, with small-scale deliveries starting this year and mass production by 2024. The venture plans to produce approximately 10,000 trucks annually, leveraging NVIDIA DRIVE Orin's high-performance compute capabilities for safe and efficient autonomous operations.

title: Pony.ai and SANY Establish Joint Venture to Develop Next Generation of Autonomous Trucks for Mass Production
summary: Pony.ai and SANY Heavy Truck have formed a strategic joint venture to develop and mass-produce next-generation Level 4 autonomous trucks. The collaboration aims to integrate Pony.ai's autonomous driving technology with SANY's heavy truck manufacturing expertise, with small-scale deliveries planned for 2022-2023 and mass production targeting 10,000 units annually by 2024. This partnership is expected to create a sophisticated intelligent logistics ecosystem, enhance road safety, reduce costs, and significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions by focusing on new energy vehicles.

title: Nomura Malaysia launches Global Shariah Semiconductor Equity Fund
summary: Nomura Asset Management Malaysia Sdn Bhd has launched its Global Shariah Semiconductor Equity Fund to provide investors access to the rapidly expanding semiconductor sector, driven by global digitalisation trends and the rollout of 5G networks. The fund aims to capitalize on the increasing demand for semiconductor chips by focusing on high-growth potential Shariah-compliant companies with strong financials and intellectual property. This fund is the first of its kind in Malaysia, with Nomura Asset Management UK Ltd acting as the investment adviser.

title: Arm: Business Strategy—SoftBank Group Report 2022
source: ソフトバンクグループ株式会社
summary: This article details Arm's business strategy as presented in the SoftBank Group Report 2022. It covers Arm's role as a global leader in semiconductor technology, its licensing business model, and strategic investments in R&D to maintain market leadership and expand into new areas like autonomous vehicles and IoT. The report highlights significant growth in both technology royalty and non-royalty revenues in fiscal 2021 and discusses the leadership transition with Rene Haas appointed as CEO.

title: Intel to produce chips for MediaTek as part of new partnership
summary: Intel will manufacture chips for MediaTek, a Taiwan-based semiconductor maker, as part of a new partnership announced today. MediaTek, a fabless chip designer, will use Intel's manufacturing facilities to produce chips for various "smart edge devices" using Intel's 16 manufacturing process. This deal is a significant achievement for Intel's Intel Foundry Services (IFS) business, which was established last year to produce chips for other companies based on their custom designs.

title: Rescale integrates Nvidia’s AI software to power digital twins for the industrial metaverse
summary: Rescale Inc. has integrated Nvidia's AI software into its platform to simplify the creation of digital twins for industrial applications, supporting the development of the "industrial metaverse." This partnership allows Rescale customers to access GPU-optimized software, including Nvidia's NGC Catalog and Modulus neural network platform, enhancing the physical accuracy of digital twins with AI-assisted engineering. The collaboration aims to accelerate innovation by providing engineers and scientists a robust foundation for building and testing designs virtually, as exemplified by Hankook Tire's use of Rescale's technology.

title: Sales of computer graphics cards slump to lowest level in two decades
summary: Sales of computer graphics cards hit a 20-year low in Q3 2022 due to a global economic slowdown and the impact of the Ethereum merge on cryptocurrency mining. Major chipmakers like AMD and Nvidia experienced significant declines in discrete desktop GPU shipments, with AMD particularly hard hit. Despite the slump, new high-end GPU launches and Intel's entry into the market (grabbing a 4% share) offer potential for future sales boosts.

title: Micron Technology Sees Chip Recovery by the End of 2023
summary: Micron Technology Inc. stock has fallen significantly in 2022 due to weak demand for DRAM chips and an oversupply in the market. Despite a challenging fiscal Q1 2023 with missed earnings and lowered guidance, Micron expects improving customer inventories to lead to increased revenue in the fiscal second half of 2023. Analysts have revised their ratings and price targets, with some maintaining overweight or buy ratings despite the current downturn.

title: Supermicro targets cloud-native workloads with new Arm-based Mt. Hamilton servers
summary: Super Micro Computer Inc. has announced an expanded lineup of Arm-based servers, dubbed Mt. Hamilton, powered by Ampere Computing LLC’s Altra and Altra Max processors. These new MegaDC servers are designed for cloud-native workloads, offering high performance per watt for applications like cloud gaming, video-on-demand, and infrastructure-as-a-service. Leveraging a single motherboard design and featuring Ampere's Arm-based CPUs with up to 128 cores, Supermicro aims to provide customers with more choices for scalable, low-latency applications.

title: NVDL Stock Fund Price and Chart — NASDAQ:NVDL
summary: This article provides detailed information about the GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF (NVDL), including its current price, performance metrics, key statistics like AUM and expense ratio, and issuer details. It also offers insights into the fund's investment strategy, classification, and answers frequently asked questions about ETFs. The analysis presents a comprehensive overview for potential investors.

title: Nvidia and Deutsche Bank team up to deliver enhanced, AI-powered financial services
summary: Nvidia and Deutsche Bank have announced a multiyear "innovation partnership" to accelerate the use of AI and machine learning in financial services. This collaboration aims to develop regulatory-compliant, AI-powered services, enhance risk model development, and accelerate Deutsche Bank's digital transformation. They will also explore AI for immersive metaverse experiences and advanced data analytics using "Finformers" to identify risks like fraud.

title: Lattice Extends Low Power Leadership with New Lattice Avant FPGA Platform
summary: Lattice Semiconductor has launched Lattice Avant, a new FPGA platform designed to extend its low-power leadership into mid-range FPGAs. This platform offers enhanced power efficiency, advanced connectivity, and optimized computing capabilities, targeting applications in Communications, Computing, Industrial, and Automotive markets. The Avant platform, beginning with the Avant-E family, aims to double Lattice's addressable market and accelerate customer designs with superior power efficiency and performance.

title: Intel says it will squeeze 1 trillion transistors onto a chip package by 2030
summary: Intel's researchers have revealed innovations in chip packaging that could lead to chips with over a trillion transistors by 2030, significantly extending Moore's Law. This development would result in computer chips ten times more powerful than current advanced silicon. The company aims to address the increasing demand for computing power driven by data consumption and AI.

title: Qubit Pharmaceuticals Accelerates Drug Discovery With Hybrid Quantum Computing
summary: Qubit Pharmaceuticals is leveraging hybrid quantum computing, combining classical and quantum computing, to significantly accelerate drug discovery. The company uses NVIDIA's QODA programming model and their Atlas software to simulate drug molecules, aiming to reduce the time and cost of identifying promising treatments for various diseases. This approach seeks to bring down the number of drug compounds needed for preclinical testing, saving substantial time and money in the pharmaceutical development process.

title: Nvidia beats revenue estimates, reassures investors
summary: Nvidia reported better-than-expected revenue for the fiscal third quarter, driven by strong demand for its AI and data-center chips, despite a slowdown in the PC market and challenges in China. The company's data center unit saw a 31% sales increase, offsetting a 51% drop in its gaming business. Although the fourth-quarter outlook was slightly below some estimates, it was sufficient to alleviate investor concerns, with CEO Jensen Huang acknowledging ongoing macroeconomic difficulties and COVID-19 restrictions in China.

title: OSS, TMGcore debut a liquid-immersion cooled transportable supercomputer featuring Nvidia GPUs
summary: One Stop Systems (OSS) and TMGcore have collaborated to launch a new two-phase liquid immersion-cooled version of the OSS Rigel Edge Supercomputer, designed for AI Transportable applications. This supercomputer, featuring Nvidia GPUs, offers efficiency, compactness, ruggedness, and high performance by using a unique immersion cooling technology that removes heat through liquid boiling, eliminating the need for fans and heatsinks. This innovation results in a smaller, more robust system with reduced power consumption and noise, ideal for autonomous vehicles, edge computing, and robotic process automation.

title: Lockheed Martin, NVIDIA to Build Digital Twin of Current Global Weather Conditions for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
summary: Lockheed Martin and NVIDIA are collaborating to create an AI-driven Earth Observations Digital Twin for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This system will efficiently monitor global environmental conditions, including extreme weather, by fusing data from various space and Earth-based sensors. The project aims to provide NOAA with a high-resolution, accurate, and timely depiction of global conditions to improve weather predictions and understanding of environmental changes.

title: Chip Maker Nvidia Issues Tepid Earnings Forecast as Videogaming Business Slows
summary: Nvidia Corp. issued a muted earnings outlook and reported a significant decline in quarterly sales, primarily due to decreased consumer demand for its videogaming chips. The company's revenue fell 17% to $5.93 billion in its fiscal third quarter, with gaming-segment sales more than halving. While sales exceeded analyst expectations, net profit at $680 million fell short.

title: Nvidia revenue falls 17% but data center growth remains strong
summary: Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter revenue fell 17% overall but its data center business saw significant growth, up 31% year-over-year. The company's gaming division sales were down 51% due to slowing demand and inventory issues. Despite beating revenue expectations, earnings per share were light, and Nvidia expects gross margin to recover in the current quarter.

title: Nvidia says it is working with Microsoft to build 'massive' cloud AI computer
summary: Nvidia Corp is partnering with Microsoft Corp to build a "massive" cloud AI computer on Microsoft's Azure cloud, utilizing thousands of Nvidia's powerful H100 and A100 GPUs. This collaboration aims to handle intense artificial intelligence computing work, driven by the increasing demand for faster processing from AI models. Nvidia will also be a customer of Microsoft's AI cloud computer, developing AI applications for its own services.

title: Nvidia and Microsoft partner to build AI supercomputer
summary: Nvidia and Microsoft are collaborating to build one of the world's most powerful AI supercomputers within Microsoft's Azure cloud platform. This partnership involves equipping Azure with tens of thousands of Nvidia's H100 GPUs and Quantum-2 network switches, along with optimizing their respective AI development tools. Nvidia will also expand its use of Azure to support its generative AI research, leveraging the platform to advance technologies like its MT-NLG system.

title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 Graphics Cards Now Available at Newegg.com
summary: Newegg Commerce, Inc. announced the availability of NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 graphics cards on Newegg.com. The RTX 4080 boasts significant performance improvements over previous generations, powered by the new NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architecture, and is also offered in pre-built ABS and MSI gaming PCs. Jim Tseng, Newegg's Director of Product Management, anticipates strong customer demand following the successful launch of the RTX 4090.

title: Industry Ministry, U.S. Firm to Cooperate on Semiconductor Industry Development
summary: Indonesia's Industry Ministry is partnering with a United States company, Zerro Power, co-founded by innovator Sehat Sutardja, to establish an integrated circuit design center. This collaboration aims to reduce Indonesia's dependence on semiconductor imports and develop an independent national semiconductor industry. The initiative is part of broader efforts to secure the semiconductor supply chain amidst increasing global demand.

title: Buffett’s Taiwan Semiconductor Stake Highlights Beaten-Down Semi Stocks
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has invested $4.1 billion in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, drawing attention to the semiconductor industry, which Morningstar analysts consider largely undervalued. Following a significant selloff in 2022 due to recession fears and U.S. restrictions on sales to China, many semiconductor companies, including Skyworks Solutions, Teradyne, and Taiwan Semiconductor, are rated as significantly undervalued. The article details Morningstar's perspectives on Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, ASML, Broadcom, and Texas Instruments, highlighting investment opportunities despite industry challenges.

title: AMD announces its reprogrammable Versal AI chips are ready for space-based deployments
summary: AMD's reprogrammable Versal AI Core chip has achieved Class B qualification, making it suitable for space-based deployments in commercial satellites. This radiation-resistant SoC enables significant advancements in onboard AI processing for satellites, offering greater performance and reconfigurability compared to traditional ASICs. Raytheon Co. is an early adopter, planning to use these chips for its next-generation space processors.

title: NVIDIA H100 and Quantum-2 Systems Announced Worldwide
summary: NVIDIA announced widespread adoption of its H100 Tensor Core GPUs and Quantum-2 InfiniBand, with offerings on Microsoft Azure and over 50 partner systems. The company also released major updates to its cuQuantum, CUDA, and BlueField DOCA acceleration libraries, and expanded Omniverse support for scientific computing. These initiatives aim to accelerate scientific discovery using a comprehensive HPC platform integrating AI and numerical methods.

title: HPE's low-end supercomputers take aim at the AI market
summary: HPE and Dell are introducing new supercomputing and high-performance computing (HPC) systems designed to meet the growing demands of AI-driven workloads. HPE is focusing on smaller, lower-cost supercomputers with advanced cooling, while Dell is enhancing its HPC offerings with powerful GPUs, aiming to make supercomputing capabilities more accessible to a broader range of enterprise users. This convergence of supercomputing and HPC is blurring the lines between the two, as both companies compete to provide infrastructure that can efficiently handle complex AI, modeling, and simulation tasks.

title: Reza Partners with Perfect Corp. to Enable Virtual Try On of Jewelry
summary: French jewelry brand Reza has collaborated with Perfect Corp. to integrate AI and AR virtual try-on technology into its new eCommerce website. This technology, featuring Perfect Corp.'s AgileHand, allows customers to virtually try on rings, earrings, and bracelets in real-time digital renderings. The partnership aims to enhance the luxury accessories shopping experience by providing an immersive and impactful virtual try-on solution.

title: AMD launches data center CPU 'Genoa', taps Google, Microsoft as customers (Nov. 10)
summary: AMD has launched its fourth-generation EPYC processor, codenamed "Genoa," for data centers, securing major customers like Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle. This new chip offers significant performance and energy efficiency improvements over its predecessor, translating into lower operational costs for enterprises and cloud data centers. The launch comes as rival Intel faces delays with its own data center chip, and AMD continues to gain market share, boosting its stock by about 14%.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Extends Supercomputing to the Enterprise with New HPE Cray Portfolio
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is expanding its supercomputing portfolio with new HPE Cray EX and HPE Cray XD supercomputers, making exascale-class technology more accessible and affordable for enterprises. These systems are designed to help businesses across various industries, including energy, finance, healthcare, and manufacturing, accelerate R&D, AI, and machine learning initiatives. The new offerings provide significant performance and AI-at-scale capabilities in smaller form factors, supporting advanced modeling, simulation, and data-intensive workloads in traditional data centers.

title: Tower Semiconductor: Opportunity or risk?
summary: Intel agreed to acquire Tower Semiconductor for $53 per share, but the market fears regulatory hurdles, especially from China and Japan, causing Tower's share price to drop significantly. The deal, valued at $5.4 billion at the time of agreement, needs approvals from multiple countries, including the US, China, Germany, Israel, Japan, the UK, and Italy. Analysts suggest that while regulatory risk exists, particularly with China due to US-China tensions, previous Israeli semiconductor acquisitions ultimately received Chinese approval, and Japan's hesitancy regarding M&A deals might be overcome as Intel plans to maintain operations there.

title: How Taiwan won the semiconductor race
summary: This article explains how Taiwan became a dominant force in the global semiconductor industry, despite starting as an agricultural economy. It attributes Taiwan's success to globalization's impact on electronics, East Asia's skilled workforce and infrastructure, and a unique business model focused on contract manufacturing rather than brand development. The piece highlights TSMC's role in supplying advanced chips globally, creating a significant dependency on Taiwan.

title: Take the Green Train: NVIDIA BlueField DPUs Drive Data Center Efficiency
summary: NVIDIA's BlueField DPUs are significantly improving data center efficiency and reducing power consumption. Tests with Ericsson, Red Hat, and VMware showed power reductions of up to 24% and performance increases up to 54x compared to CPUs, by offloading networking, security, and storage tasks. These advancements contribute to substantial cost savings and align with the growing need for green computing solutions.

title: Jaguar Land Rover Secures Semi Conductor Chips For Future Electric Cars
summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has formed a strategic partnership with Wolfspeed, Inc. to secure Silicon Carbide semiconductors for its next-generation electric vehicles. This collaboration aims to enhance powertrain efficiency and extend driving range for JLR's upcoming electric models, with the first Range Rover vehicles featuring this technology expected in 2024. The partnership is a key part of JLR's "Reimagine" strategy to become carbon net zero by 2039.

title: Micron Ships World's Most Advanced DRAM Technology With 1-Beta Node
summary: Micron Technology has announced it is shipping qualification samples of its 1β (1-beta) DRAM technology to select smartphone manufacturers and chipset partners, achieving mass production readiness for the world's most advanced DRAM technology node. This LPDDR5X mobile memory delivers top speeds of 8.5 gigabits per second, with significant gains in power efficiency (15% improvement) and bit density (over 35% improvement) at 16Gb per die capacity. The 1β node is poised to support highly responsive applications from mobile to data centers and intelligent vehicles, stemming from Micron's pioneering R&D and nanomanufacturing capabilities.

title: Arm Could Change Licensing Model to Charge OEMs Directly
summary: Arm might change its licensing model by requiring OEMs to license almost all of its IP if they wish to use its CPU IP, directly challenging existing deals and potentially pushing chipmakers toward alternatives like RISC-V. This potential shift, revealed through Qualcomm's counterclaim in a legal dispute, would prevent mixing Arm's IP with other companies' designs (e.g., AMD GPUs in Samsung chips). The change is expected to take effect in 2025, with exemptions for long-term licensees like NVIDIA and Apple.

title: Qualcomm Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) fell 2.89% on Thursday, closing at $114.70, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose and the S&P 500 Index fell. This marked the stock's second consecutive day of losses and positioned it below its 52-week high. Qualcomm underperformed some competitors like NVIDIA Corp. and Cisco Systems Inc., though it fared slightly better than Alphabet Inc. Class A.

title: Lowe’s opens tech hub
summary: Lowe's has opened a new 357,000-sq.-ft. tech hub in Charlotte, N.C., centralizing its technology development activities to support its goal of becoming the most customer-centric omnichannel retailer. The facility, designed for innovation and collaboration, will employ up to 2,000 tech professionals and focus on projects like its interactive virtual store models ("digital twins") and the "Measure Your Space" app feature. This move aligns with Lowe's commitment to leveraging emerging technology to evolve its brand and services.

title: Mobileye pops more than 37% in market debut after spinning out of Intel
summary: Mobileye, Intel's self-driving car technology company, saw its shares surge over 37% in its stock market debut after spinning out of Intel. The IPO, which valued Mobileye at around $17 billion, raised $861 million, with Intel planning to use some proceeds to build chip factories. This market debut provides a notable tech IPO in a slow year, despite Mobileye's valuation being below Intel's initial expectations.

title: Rambus announces next-gen PCIe 6.0 interface for data centers, AI systems
summary: Rambus has unveiled its next-generation PCIe 6.0 Interface Subsystem, designed for high-performance data centers and AI SoCs, offering speeds up to 64 GT/s. This subsystem includes PHY and controller IP, supports CXL 3.0, and is optimized for advanced heterogeneous computing architectures with features like an Integrity and Data Encryption engine. It ensures compatibility with previous PCIe generations while introducing innovations like low-latency Forward Error Correction.

title: Rambus Announces PCIe 6.0: Powering Next-Gen High-Performance Data Center & AI Solutions
summary: Rambus has unveiled its new PCIe 6.0 interface subsystem, an advanced solution designed for the next generation of data centers and AI applications. This subsystem, comprising PHY and controller IP, delivers data rates up to 64 GT/s and supports the latest CXL 3.0 specification for enhanced memory sharing and pooling. It features an Integrity and Data Encryption (IDE) engine for data protection and is backward compatible with previous PCIe generations.

title: China’s Biren GPUs Can’t Be Made at TSMC Due To US Regulations & Competition With NVIDIA
summary: Birentech, a Chinese chip startup, is reportedly barred from manufacturing its Biren GPUs at TSMC due to US regulations aimed at restricting China's access to advanced AI and datacenter chips. This decision is influenced by the Biren BR100's potential to outperform NVIDIA's A100 chips, which are already banned for the Chinese market, and could severely impact Birentech's manufacturing plans.

title: 7 Virtual Reality Stocks to Buy to Bet on the Coming VR Boom
summary: The virtual reality market is projected to grow significantly to over $227 billion by 2029, presenting a massive opportunity for investors, especially as many top VR stocks are currently oversold. This article highlights seven virtual reality stocks to consider, including the ProShares Metaverse ETF (VERS) for diversification, Roblox (RBLX) as a leading social metaverse platform, and tech giants like Microsoft (MSFT) and Apple (AAPL) that are heavily investing in VR/AR. Other recommendations include Nvidia (NVDA) for its Omniverse platform, Matterport (MTTR) for its exposure to "digital twins," and Unity Software (U) which recently received a "buy" rating.

title: Oracle Cloud adds NVIDIA chips, software to speed enterprise AI uptake
summary: Oracle has expanded its partnership with NVIDIA to integrate tens of thousands of NVIDIA's AI-processing graphics chips and software tools into Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This aims to accelerate enterprise AI adoption across industries like banking, healthcare, and manufacturing by offering powerful A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs. The collaboration will also provide access to NVIDIA software like RAPIDS Accelerator and Clara for enhanced AI performance, medical imaging, and drug discovery.

title: Oracle and NVIDIA Partner to Speed AI Adoption for Enterprises
summary: Oracle and NVIDIA have expanded their long-standing alliance through a multi-year partnership aimed at accelerating AI adoption for enterprises. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) will significantly increase its GPU capacity with NVIDIA's A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs, supporting the full stack of NVIDIA AI software and services. This collaboration will provide enterprises with a broad, accessible portfolio for AI training and deep learning inference, integrating NVIDIA AI platforms into OCI to drive innovation across various industries.

title: Adobe Advances 3D, Immersive and Metaverse Experiences With New Products
summary: Adobe announced significant advancements in its Substance 3D tools, introducing new products like 3D Capture and Substance 3D Modeler to facilitate the creation of 3D and metaverse-ready immersive experiences. The company also revealed a partnership with Meta to integrate Substance 3D tools into the Quest platform, making 3D content creation more accessible. These innovations aim to support creators and brands in transitioning into new mediums, emphasizing ease of use and sustainability with a new Substance 3D Sustainability Calculator.

title: Supermicro Extends Best of Breed Server Building Block Solutions to Include a Broad Set of OCP Technologies - Driving Customer Innovation and Time-to-Market
summary: Supermicro is expanding its server portfolio to incorporate open hardware and open-source technologies, aiming to drive innovation and reduce proprietary lock-in for customers. These solutions, including an 8U 8-GPU AI training system and OCP 3.0 compliant AIOM cards, integrate best-in-class components like Intel, AMD, and ARM CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, alongside open technologies such as OpenBMC and Open BIOS. This initiative provides customers with high-performance, efficient, and flexible server options for various applications, from cloud and AI/ML to storage and 5G/Edge computing.

title: Samsung, Qualcomm unveil industry’s fastest LPDDR5X DRAM chip
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. has successfully demonstrated the performance of its LPDDR5X DRAM on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon mobile platform, achieving an industry-leading speed of 8.5 gigabits per second (Gbps). This advancement surpasses Samsung's previous record and solidifies its leadership in the memory market. The new high-speed, low-power memory is expected to enhance mobile, gaming, camera, and AI applications and find broader use in PCs, HPC, servers, and autonomous driving.

title: Gartner Top 10 Tech Trends For 2023: Metaverse, AI, Cloud
summary: Gartner has released its top 10 technology trends for 2023, focusing on themes like optimizing resilience, scaling solutions, and pioneering new opportunities amidst economic uncertainty. The trends include the metaverse, super apps, adaptive AI, industry cloud platforms, and sustainability, emphasizing technology's role in addressing global challenges and driving business value beyond just cost savings. Each trend is accompanied by an example of its real-world application.

title: Credo Announces 1.6Tbps OSFP-XD HiWire AECs Targeting Hyperscaler Spine Switching
summary: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd announced its new 1.6Tb OSFP-XD HiWire CLOS Active Electrical Cable (AEC), designed for hyperscale data centers requiring high-density spine switching. This AEC supports speeds up to 1.6Tbps, cable lengths up to 2.75m, and consumes less than 20W of power, making it energy-efficient and suitable for next-generation 51.2Tbps switches in a 1U form factor. The product leverages a 12nm process for cost-effectiveness and is being showcased at the OCP Summit.

title: Nvidia closes Russian offices, will fly relocating employees out of the country, report says
summary: Nvidia is ceasing all activities and closing its offices in Russia, offering its employees the opportunity to relocate out of the country. The company had previously suspended shipments to Russia but maintained an office to support employees and their families. Nvidia stated that recent developments have made it impossible to operate effectively there.

title: As NVIDIA Corporation's (NASDAQ:NVDA)) market cap dropped by US$9.4b, insiders who sold US$156m worth of stock were able to offset their losses
summary: Insiders at NVIDIA Corporation sold US$156 million worth of stock over the last year at an average price of US$212 per share, effectively offsetting some losses as the company's market cap dropped by US$9.4 billion. While insider selling occurred, the notable sale by Independent Director Mark Stevens was at a price well above the current stock price, making strong conclusions difficult. Insiders collectively own about 4.0% of the company, valued at US$12 billion, which is seen as a positive sign of alignment with shareholders despite a lack of recent insider buying.

title: Meet the Harvard Law School graduate helping China cut its reliance on US AI chips
summary: Michael Zhang Wen, a Harvard Law School graduate and chairman of Biren Technology, is leading China's efforts to reduce its dependence on US artificial intelligence (AI) chips. His Shanghai-based start-up recently released the BR100, a 7-nanometre GPU, which some believe could position Biren to become "China's Nvidia" amidst escalating US export restrictions on advanced chips. Zhang faces pressure to deliver, as his company has raised a substantial US$655 million from major venture capital funds.

title: TSMC starts mass-producing three-nanometer chips
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (TSMC) has begun mass-producing processors using its advanced three-nanometer chip technology. This new technology offers a 15% improvement in chip performance and up to 35% less power consumption compared to its earlier five-nanometer process. TSMC, a major contract chip manufacturer for companies like Apple, AMD, and Nvidia, plans to develop multiple versions of this technology and is building new fabrication plants in Arizona.

title: How the industrial metaverse will transform manufacturing
summary: The industrial metaverse, leveraging virtual and augmented reality, is transforming manufacturing by enhancing training, collaboration, and the use of digital twins. Companies like Lincoln Electric are using VR for faster and more efficient welder training, while automotive manufacturers like Kia and Volvo are using metaverse technologies for remote design collaboration and virtual prototyping, significantly cutting down development time and costs. Despite challenges like high equipment costs and technical difficulties, the industrial metaverse is gaining traction, with its applications expected to expand beyond initial consumer-focused visions.

title: The bright side of the chip glut: Nvidia, AMD and Intel gaming cards are cheap and very available for Christmas
summary: The article highlights that due to a chip glut, gaming cards from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel are now readily available and significantly discounted, making them an affordable option for Christmas shoppers. This marks a significant change from the previous two years when these items were scarce and expensive. The availability addresses past disappointments for gamers hoping for these cards during the holidays.

title: Alibaba Cloud cuts prices by up to 50% for core, storage products
summary: Alibaba Cloud, the cloud computing division of Alibaba Group, announced price cuts of up to 50% on its core products and services to increase its market share in China amidst growing competition. This move, effective Wednesday, includes reductions for services using Arm, Intel-based chips, and Nvidia GPUs. The company also revealed that over 200,000 enterprises have requested beta testing for its AI-powered large language model, Tongyi Qianwen.

title: NVIDIA Enables Trustworthy, Safe, and Secure Large Language Model Conversational Systems
summary: NVIDIA has introduced NeMo Guardrails, an open-source toolkit designed to ensure the safety, security, and trustworthiness of large language model (LLM) conversational systems. This toolkit allows developers to define programmable rules, known as guardrails, that guide user interactions and prevent off-topic discussions, misinformation, toxicity, and malicious code execution. NeMo Guardrails integrates with existing LLMs and toolkits like LangChain, providing a robust framework for building reliable AI applications.

title: Cognitive Computing Brings Human Touch
summary: Cognitive computing, particularly neuromorphic computing, is poised to transform artificial intelligence by enabling systems to "think" like humans, learn from data, and interact naturally. This technology, which uses artificial neurons to mimic the human brain, could power various applications from autonomous vehicles to smart devices with greater efficiency. While companies developing this technology present investment opportunities, the article suggests that adopting companies leveraging it for increased productivity and growth may offer even greater upside, while also highlighting the ethical considerations and risks associated with advanced AI systems.

title: Prime Minister Pashinyan receives the President and CEO of Nvidia company Jensen Huang
summary: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan met with Jensen Huang, President and CEO of Nvidia, a leader in the high-tech sector. The discussion focused on the development of engineering education, the advancement of the high-tech sector, and continued collaboration between the Armenian government and Nvidia. Nvidia had established a scientific research center in Armenia the previous year, with both parties expressing commitment to further development in the country's IT sector.

title: Alibaba's Hong Kong shares slump on SoftBank's stake sale report
summary: Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares fell significantly following reports that SoftBank Group Corp is selling almost all of its remaining stake in the Chinese e-commerce giant. This move comes as valuations for China's big tech firms are recovering after a period of heightened regulatory scrutiny and as SoftBank seeks to monetize profitable holdings amidst efforts to shore up cash reserves for its Vision Fund losses. SoftBank has been shifting to a "defensive mode" and had previously booked a substantial gain by cutting its Alibaba stake last year.

title: 2 Under-The-Radar Small Chip Stocks Poised For Big Growth
summary: This article highlights two under-the-radar fabless semiconductor companies, Impinj Inc. (NASDAQ: PI) and Allegro MicroSystems, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALGM), that are showing strong growth potential despite being smaller players in the chip industry. Both companies are experiencing increasing sales and earnings, with analysts expecting continued growth in the coming years. The article details their specific market niches and financial performance, positioning them as attractive opportunities for investors.

title: Qualcomm, Nvidia spar for top spot in AI chip efficiency tests
summary: Qualcomm's AI 100 chips outperformed Nvidia's H100 chips in two out of three power efficiency categories for AI inference tasks, specifically image classification and object detection. Nvidia, however, took the lead in natural language processing performance and power efficiency. This highlights the competitive landscape in the growing market for data center inference chips, where power consumption is a key cost factor.

title: Best-Performing Stocks of Q1 2023
summary: The first quarter of 2023 saw a significant rebound in technology and communication services stocks, with Nvidia, Meta Platforms, and Salesforce among the top performers. This resurgence was driven by factors such as better-than-expected earnings, cost-cutting measures, and growing enthusiasm for artificial intelligence, contrasting sharply with the downturn experienced in 2022. Other sectors like entertainment and media, cryptocurrency, and electric vehicles also saw notable gains.

title: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) Stock: Breakout Leveraging Tech Stocks Rally?
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) ETF has shown a positive resurgence in 2023, largely driven by gains in tech and semiconductor stocks, which comprise a significant portion of its portfolio. Technical analysis suggests a potential bullish breakout for SPY, with indicators pointing to an upcoming rally. Investors are advised to watch support levels and anticipate a rise leveraging the strength of its underlying tech holdings.

title: Synopsys Launches Full-Stack, AI-Driven EDA Suite
summary: Synopsys has introduced Synopsys.ai, a comprehensive AI-driven suite of solutions for the entire chip design process, from architecture to manufacturing. This suite enables engineers to leverage AI at every stage and access tools via the cloud, significantly reducing product development time and improving silicon performance. Leading semiconductor companies, including Renesas, MediaTek, IBM Research, and TSMC, are already utilizing Synopsys.ai to optimize design, verification, testing, and manufacturing, demonstrating the transformative potential of AI in the semiconductor industry.

title: Synopsys.ai Unveiled as Industry's First Full-Stack, AI-Driven EDA Suite for Chipmakers
summary: Synopsys launched Synopsys.ai, an AI-driven EDA suite for chip design, verification, testing, and manufacturing. This suite allows engineers to use AI at every stage of chip development, significantly boosting productivity, silicon quality, and cost reduction. Market leaders like NVIDIA, TSMC, IBM, MediaTek, and Renesas have tested and supported Synopsys' AI strategy, reporting substantial benefits and efficiency improvements.

title: Supermicro Expands GPU Solutions Portfolio with Deskside Liquid-Cooled AI Development Platform, Powered by NVIDIA
summary: Supermicro has launched a new liquid-cooled AI development platform, the SYS-751GE-TNRT-NV1, designed for deskside use. This platform features four NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs and two 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs, providing a powerful, quiet, and energy-efficient solution for AI/HPC workloads. It also includes a three-year subscription to NVIDIA AI Enterprise, simplifying software setup for developers.

title: Liquid Cooled AI Development Platform
summary: Supermicro has launched a new liquid-cooled AI development platform, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, designed for advanced AI developers. This system features four liquid-cooled NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering over 2 Petaflops of AI performance in a quiet, self-contained unit suitable for various environments. It is available with optional NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and can be customized to specific requirements.

title: AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF (LOWV), which was established on March 22, 2023. The ETF focuses on large- and mid-cap US stocks, actively managed to achieve lower volatility than the broader market. Key holdings include major technology companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, and Amazon, alongside diversified investments across various sectors.

title: Raja Koduri, Main Driver Of Intel’s GPU Efforts, To Leave Company
summary: Raja Koduri, Intel's chief architect and the main driver behind its discrete GPU efforts, is leaving the company at the end of March to start a new software company focused on generative AI for gaming, media, and entertainment. Koduri had been with Intel for over five years, leading the buildout of its graphics capabilities and serving as chief architect for most of his tenure. His departure comes as Intel announced cuts to its data center GPU roadmap and delays to Falcon Shores.

title: Demo of China’s Answer to ChatGPT Disappoints Investors
summary: Baidu Inc.'s CEO Robin Li unveiled "Ernie Bot," China's answer to ChatGPT, in a recorded video demonstration that disappointed investors, leading to a 6.4% drop in Baidu's shares. The pre-recorded nature of the demo and lack of real-time interaction raised questions about Ernie's capabilities compared to OpenAI's ChatGPT. Despite the initial disappointment, Baidu is considered a frontrunner in China's AI race, planning to integrate Ernie Bot across its services while navigating concerns about US tech restrictions and Chinese regulatory oversight.

title: Deal Roundup: WeRide files for $500m US listing
summary: WeRide, an autonomous driving technology developer, has confidentially filed for a US IPO aiming to raise up to $500M, with several corporate investors poised for an exit. The deal roundup also highlights CNH Industrial's $110M acquisition of Augmenta Agriculture Technologies and Vivasure Medical's €30M series D funding. Additionally, it details a new €50M fund from Rethink Ventures backed by multiple corporates and various other recent funding rounds across different sectors.

title: Ssangyong E&C wins contract for building ASML Korea campus
summary: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction secured a 200-billion-won ($170-million) contract to build a new campus for ASML Holding NV in Hwaseong, South Korea. The campus, with two buildings totaling 74,418 square meters, will house offices and research facilities for ASML, specializing in extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment. This project aims to expand ASML's local supply chain and customer support by enabling more parts procurement in Korea and expanding its partner firm base.

title: Rockwell Automation acquires Knowledge Lens
summary: Rockwell Automation has acquired Bengaluru-based enterprise insights provider Knowledge Lens for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition aims to boost Rockwell's capabilities in data utilization, autonomous manufacturing, and continuous optimization for manufacturers worldwide. Knowledge Lens will join Rockwell's digital services business, Kalypso, to accelerate transformational outcomes for its global clientele, aligning with Rockwell's strategy to expand capabilities and explore early-stage investments in India.

title: Microchip Technology, microchip manufacturer with capital of $50 billion, coming to Armenia
summary: American microchip manufacturer Microchip Technology, with a market capital of $50 billion, is expanding its operations into Armenia. This follows a two-year collaborative agreement with Instigate company, which culminated in Microchip Technology acquiring Instigate Semiconductor. The move is part of a larger trend of major tech and energy companies, including NVIDIA, AMD, and Shell, establishing a presence in Armenia, aiming to boost the country's productivity, innovation, and expertise in high-tech fields.

title: HP CEO Lores: Hybrid Work Is ‘Driving Innovation Across Our Portfolio’
summary: HP CEO Enrique Lores stated that hybrid work is a long-term trend fueling innovation across their portfolio, with their hybrid systems business more than doubling year over year. Despite a general economic downturn and weakening corporate demand impacting PC sales, the company maintains its fiscal year outlook and expects to achieve significant cost savings. HP is also expanding its subscription services and investing in areas like AI and professional workstations.

title: BBLU Top Holdings List & Exposure (EA Bridgeway Blue Chip ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure breakdown for the EA Bridgeway Blue Chip ETF (BBLU). It lists the top 25 stock holdings by weight, including Broadcom, NVIDIA, and JPMorgan Chase & Co., which collectively comprise over 73% of the fund. Additionally, the article provides a comprehensive analysis of BBLU's geographic, currency, sector, and industry exposure, revealing a 100% focus on the United States and USD, with significant allocations to Technology and Financials.

title: Applied Materials stock rises on new chip-making system that helps lower costs
summary: Applied Materials Inc. shares rose after the company unveiled a new chip-making system designed to lower manufacturing costs for semiconductors. The system, called Centura Sculpta, promises to save fabs like TSMC and Intel $50 per wafer. This innovation led to a notable outperformance of Applied Materials stock compared to its peers and the broader semiconductor market.

title: The Future of AI Stocks: 7 Companies to Keep Your Eye On
summary: This article identifies seven key AI stocks and ETFs that investors should consider due to artificial intelligence's potential to revolutionize various industries. It highlights companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Advanced Micro Devices for their direct involvement in AI technology, along with Innodata and C3.ai for their specific AI solutions. Additionally, it suggests AI-focused ETFs like ROBO Global Artificial Intelligence ETF and Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF for diversified investment in the burgeoning AI sector.

title: This Week in the Metaverse: BlackRock's new ETF, Titanic artifacts as NFTs, and a Snow Crash Sotheby’s auction
summary: BlackRock has launched a new metaverse ETF, allowing investors to engage with companies contributing to virtual platforms, gaming, and AR/VR. In other news, never-before-seen photos of rapper Tupac Shakur are being released as NFTs, while artifacts from the Titanic will also be preserved and sold as NFTs. Additionally, Sotheby's is holding an auction to celebrate 30 years of Neal Stephenson's "Snow Crash," featuring physical and digital items tied to the seminal metaverse novel.

title: Intel Corp. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Shares of Intel Corp. (INTC) increased by 0.55% to $25.61 on Thursday, outperforming the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which rose 0.53% and 0.33% respectively. This rise ended a four-day losing streak for Intel, although the stock remains significantly below its 52-week high. Despite the overall positive day for Intel, it underperformed some competitors like NVIDIA Corp.

title: As chatbots boom, Nvidia sales outlook beats Wall Street expectations
summary: Nvidia Corp (NVDA.O) surpassed Wall Street's first-quarter revenue expectations, driven by a surge in demand for its chips used in AI services like chatbots. The company announced a new cloud computing service to help businesses develop generative AI, positioning itself to significantly benefit from the growing AI sector despite a broader downturn in the PC market. Analysts project this boom in generative AI could add an additional $14 billion to Nvidia's revenue by 2027.

title: Meet the $10,000 Nvidia chip powering the race for A.I.
summary: The Nvidia A100 chip, costing around $10,000, has become a critical tool in the artificial intelligence industry, powering applications like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. Nvidia dominates the market for GPUs used in machine learning, with the A100 serving as a "workhorse" for AI professionals and requiring substantial investment for companies to train and deploy AI models. Despite the high costs and emerging competition, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang asserts that their GPUs offer a much more affordable solution for developing sophisticated AI models compared to traditional CPU-based data centers.

title: Nvidia adds to AI hype with new cloud-based service, stock jumps on forecast
summary: Nvidia's shares surged after the company announced strong fiscal fourth-quarter results and plans to make its AI software available on major cloud platforms like Oracle, Microsoft, and Alphabet. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the potential of their new browser-based DGX Cloud AI supercomputer service to accelerate adoption of higher-margin data-center software, capitalizing on the booming interest in artificial intelligence. This move is expected to expand the chip maker's revenue streams beyond hardware.

title: Nvidia earnings overshadowed by Microsoft, ChatGPT, OpenAI, 10-year gaming partnership
summary: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is largely overshadowed by its new 10-year partnership with Microsoft to bring Activision Blizzard and Xbox games to GeForce Now. This partnership also highlights Nvidia's role in powering AI technologies like OpenAI's ChatGPT, especially given Microsoft's recent investment in OpenAI and plans to integrate its AI across services. The focus is now on Nvidia's data-center sales and its contribution from public cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure.

title: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Nintendo in 10-year deal to stream Xbox games
summary: Microsoft has secured 10-year agreements with Nvidia and Nintendo to stream Xbox games as part of its strategy to address antitrust concerns regarding its proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This partnership aims to make Xbox and potential Activision titles available on Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service and Nintendo platforms, covering various devices. The move is intended to placate regulators scrutinizing the $69 billion deal.

title: Microsoft and NVIDIA Announce Expansive New Gaming Deal
summary: Microsoft and NVIDIA have announced a 10-year partnership to bring Xbox PC games, including Activision Blizzard titles like Call of Duty, to NVIDIA's GeForce NOW cloud gaming service. This agreement will allow over 25 million GeForce NOW members to stream these games across various devices and resolves NVIDIA's concerns regarding Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, leading NVIDIA to support the regulatory approval of the merger. The collaboration aims to expand gaming choices and make popular titles more accessible through cloud streaming.

title: NVIDIA GTC 2023 to Feature Latest Advances in AI Computing Systems, Generative AI, Industrial Metaverse, Robotics; Keynote by Jensen Huang; Talks by OpenAI, DeepMind Founders
summary: NVIDIA announced its GTC 2023 conference, scheduled for March 20-23, will feature a keynote by CEO Jensen Huang focusing on generative AI, the metaverse, large language models, and robotics. The virtual event expects over 250,000 registrants and more than 650 sessions, including talks from leaders like OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. GTC 2023 will also offer learning opportunities, dedicated sessions for startups, and a financial analyst Q&A session.

summary: Equinix has implemented two-phase liquid cooling on live production servers for its Metal infrastructure-as-a-service offering, using ZutaCore technology. This system, which involves a fluid boiling and condensing to remove heat more efficiently, has been running stably for six months in its NY5 data center. The company is testing this on standard hardware to prepare for higher thermal design power (TDP) servers and address potential future industry needs for more efficient cooling solutions, despite current PUE metrics not fully capturing its benefits.

summary: NVIDIA has released NeMo Guardrails, new open-source software designed to help developers ensure generative AI applications, particularly those powered by large language models, remain accurate, appropriate, on-topic, and secure. This software enables the creation of topical, safety, and security guardrails to prevent AI from veering off course, filtering unwanted language, and restricting connections to safe third-party applications. NeMo Guardrails is compatible with various developer tools like LangChain and Zapier, and is integrated into the NVIDIA NeMo framework, which can also be accessed as part of the NVIDIA AI Enterprise platform or as a service.

summary: Google has released new details about its custom-designed Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) supercomputers, claiming they are faster and more power-efficient than Nvidia's A100 chip systems. This advancement enables real-time optimization for live video streams, reducing storage and bitrate while maintaining high visual quality. Beamr is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop a cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) offering, with a beta launch planned for Q3 2023, aiming to attract new customers with competitive pricing.
