title: Oracle surges, chip stocks rise as Trump unveils $500 bln AI plan
summary: Oracle's shares jumped nearly 9% after former President Donald Trump announced a $500 billion AI infrastructure investment plan, "Stargate," involving Oracle, OpenAI, and SoftBank to keep the U.S. competitive in the global AI race. Other technology partners and AI-related companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Arm, Vistra, Dell Technologies, Super Micro Computer, and Palantir Technologies, also saw their stock prices increase following the news. The plan includes an immediate $100 billion investment, with the remaining over the next four years, and construction of data centers already underway in Texas.

title: People are buying the wrong stock thinking it's part of OpenAI's Stargate Project
summary: A biotechnology company named Metagenomi (MGX) saw its stock price surge by as much as 33% due to investor confusion, as many believed it was involved in OpenAI and SoftBank's new "Stargate Project." The actual MGX involved is a technology fund from the UAE, not the biotech firm. The Stargate Project aims to invest $500 billion in AI infrastructure, with figures like Donald Trump, Sam Altman, and Masayoshi Son backing it, though some, like Elon Musk and Gavin Baker, have expressed skepticism about the funding claims.

The company is also advancing its 1,400MW Sweetwater data center project, targeting energization in April 2026, and actively exploring a multi-gigawatt development pipeline to enhance its portfolio of power and land resources. These initiatives are supported by a new $1 billion at-the-market facility and a focus on optimal capital sources.

summary: MicroStrategy is seeking shareholder approval to dramatically increase its authorized Class A common shares from 330 million to 10.3 billion, a move that would position it with more shares outstanding than many Nasdaq 100 tech giants. This expansion is designed to fuel its aggressive Bitcoin acquisition strategy, which has already seen its stock surge over 2,500% since 2020. Despite potential dilution concerns, investors appear to prioritize the company's Bitcoin-centric growth.

title: AMD: Trading at a 20% Discount, This Misunderstood Stock Is a Buy | Morningstar UK
summary: Morningstar believes Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is undervalued, trading at a 20% discount to its fair value estimate despite a challenging 2024. The company is well-positioned in the lucrative AI chip market, second only to Nvidia, and its strong data center business is expected to drive significant growth. Morningstar maintains a "narrow economic moat" rating for AMD, citing its chip design expertise and its unique x86 instruction set architecture license.

summary: Supermicro is showcasing its latest AI server, storage, and edge computing solutions for the retail industry at the National Retail Federation (NRF) annual show, in collaboration with NVIDIA. These solutions aim to enhance retail operations, security, and efficiency by leveraging generative AI for personalized shopping, logistical automation, and shrinkage prevention. Supermicro highlights its broad portfolio of edge AI solutions and various server systems designed to deliver high-end performance at retail locations, demonstrating use cases like digital human customer service, AI shopping assistants, and video search for loss prevention.

summary: US stock prices fell following stronger-than-expected employment numbers, highlighting investor concerns that positive economic news could lead to stickier inflation and fewer interest rate cuts in 2025. Upcoming inflation data and Taiwan Semiconductor earnings are expected to influence market volatility.

title: NVIDIA Statement on the Biden Administration’s Misguided ‘AI Diffusion’ Rule
summary: NVIDIA expresses strong disapproval of the Biden Administration's new "AI Diffusion" rule, arguing it will stifle innovation and economic growth by restricting mainstream computing applications. The company contends that this overreach undermines America's technological leadership and global competitiveness, advocating for policies that promote innovation and open competition instead.

summary: IQVIA and NVIDIA have announced a strategic collaboration to advance AI solutions in healthcare and life sciences, leveraging IQVIA’s data and expertise with NVIDIA’s AI Foundry service. This partnership aims to accelerate IQVIA Healthcare-grade AI™ by developing agentic AI solutions to automate complex workflows and improve patient outcomes. Initial solutions are expected to reach the market within the calendar year, utilizing NVIDIA's advanced AI technologies and platforms.

title: NVIDIA Announces Blueprint for AI Retail Shopping Assistants
summary: NVIDIA has introduced the NVIDIA AI Blueprint for retail shopping assistants, a generative AI workflow aimed at enhancing online and in-store shopping experiences. This blueprint, built on NVIDIA AI Enterprise and Omniverse platforms, empowers developers to create AI-powered digital assistants capable of tasks like understanding text/image prompts, searching multiple items, and presenting products in virtual environments. The initiative seeks to improve customer satisfaction, boost conversion rates, and reduce returns by providing personalized and intelligent shopping assistance.

title: AMD invests $20M in AI-powered drug discovery company Absci
summary: AMD has invested $20 million in Absci Corp., an AI-powered company focused on drug discovery, and will also partner with them on research. Absci, which uses artificial intelligence to identify therapeutic proteins and epitopes, will shift some of its workloads to AMD's Instinct AI processors and utilize AMD's ROCm software. This collaboration aims to enhance Absci's AI models and develop new hardware and software optimized for the healthcare sector, particularly in drug discovery.

title: Astera Labs to triple the size of its Silicon Valley headquarters
summary: Astera Labs, an AI firm, is set to triple the size of its Silicon Valley headquarters by leasing a 154,200 square-foot office complex in north San Jose. The move, expected in spring, allows the company to relocate from its current 51,300 square-foot Santa Clara office and accommodate its rapid growth following a significant IPO in March 2024. This expansion highlights the continued strength of the technology sector in driving large office leases in Silicon Valley.

title: Ceva Expands Embedded AI NPU Ecosystem with New Partnerships That Accelerate Time-to-Market for Smart Edge Devices
summary: Ceva, Inc. announced new partnerships with Cyberon Corporation and AIZIP, expanding its embedded AI ecosystem for the Ceva-NeuPro-Nano NPU. These collaborations aim to accelerate time-to-market for smart edge devices by offering pre-optimized AI models for tasks like keyword spotting and face recognition. Additionally, Ceva's partnership with Edge Impulse now includes full integration of Edge Impulse Studio and support for NVIDIA's TAO Toolkit, further simplifying and speeding up AI application development and deployment.

summary: Baidu, often referred to as the "Google of China," is rapidly transforming into an AI powerhouse, with its ERNIE Bot and Apollo autonomous driving platform gaining significant traction. summary: The article reviews the best and worst-performing ETFs of 2024, highlighting that trends from the previous year, particularly the strong performance of tech and blockchain ETFs, largely continued. summary: Arbe Robotics (Nasdaq: ARBE; TASE: ARBE) saw its stock jump 64% after announcing a collaboration with Nvidia. The Israeli auto-tech chip company will integrate its high-resolution radar with Nvidia DRIVE AGX to enhance free space mapping and AI-driven capabilities for advanced automotive safety and autonomous driving. This partnership will be showcased at CES 2025, and the stock surge has pushed Arbe's share price above a critical $3.1 threshold required for a convertible bond transfer.

title: Intel Extends Leadership in AI PCs and Edge Computing at CES 2025
summary: At CES 2025, Intel unveiled new Intel Core Ultra (Series 2) processors, including the 200V series with Intel vPro for businesses, and 200HX and H series for creators and gamers, all featuring cutting-edge AI enhancements and performance improvements. Intel also introduced a new suite of processors for edge computing, showcasing significant performance gains in AI workloads compared to previous generations and competitors. The availability of these new systems is set to begin in January and February 2025, with further releases planned for the first half of the year.

summary: Soluna Holdings, Inc. announced a deal with Atlas Cloud to provide sustainable AI video processing services, utilizing 64 Nvidia H100 GPUs with potential for expansion. This partnership, secured through Soluna's collaboration with HPE GreenLake, marks Soluna's second AI customer and highlights its commitment to delivering renewable-powered cloud services for intensive computing applications. The agreement reinforces Atlas Cloud's mission to offer a sustainable, one-stop AI cloud platform for various industry verticals.

summary: NVIDIA announced the launch of foundation models for RTX AI PCs, designed to power digital humans, content creation, productivity, and development. These models, offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices, are accelerated by new GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, featuring significant AI performance and supporting FP4 compute for enhanced inference. NVIDIA is collaborating with top PC manufacturers to integrate these NIM-ready RTX AI PCs, emphasizing the company's commitment to advancing AI accessibility for developers and enthusiasts.

title: NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Platform Achieves Critical Automotive Safety and Cybersecurity Milestones for AV Development
summary: The NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion autonomous vehicle platform has achieved critical automotive safety and cybersecurity milestones, receiving certifications from TÜV SÜD and TÜV Rheinland. This platform, adopted by automotive manufacturers like Mercedes-Benz and JLR, will feature the high-performance DRIVE AGX Thor SoC built on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture. summary: NVIDIA has introduced Project DIGITS, a personal AI supercomputer powered by the new GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, designed to bring powerful AI computing capabilities to researchers, data scientists, and students. This desktop system offers a petaflop of AI performance for developing and running large AI models, which can then be seamlessly deployed to cloud or data center infrastructures. With a starting price of $3,000, Project DIGITS aims to democratize access to advanced AI development tools, fostering innovation in the field.

summary: At CES 2025, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang announced several innovations, emphasizing the shift towards "physical AI" that can perceive, reason, plan, and act. Key reveals included the NVIDIA Cosmos platform for physical AI, new Blackwell-based GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, and AI tools for RTX PCs. Huang highlighted partnerships with companies like Toyota and Uber, and introduced Project DIGITS, NVIDIA's smallest yet most powerful AI supercomputer, underscoring AI's rapid advancement across gaming, robotics, and autonomous vehicles.

summary: NVIDIA has announced its new GeForce RTX 50 Series Desktop and Laptop GPUs, powered by the Blackwell architecture, which aim to revolutionize AI computer graphics. summary: Camtek, an Israeli manufacturer of inspection systems for the semiconductor industry, has seen its stock price break the $100 milestone, achieving a market value exceeding $4 billion. This significant growth, including a 265% increase over the last year, is attributed to high demand from the semiconductor and AI markets, particularly in areas like High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and Advanced Packaging. The company's strong performance and profitability highlight its crucial role in ensuring chip quality for leading manufacturers amidst a rapidly evolving tech landscape.

title: COMPUTEX 2024 News
summary: NVIDIA's COMPUTEX 2024 news features CEO Jensen Huang's "Accelerate Everything" message and a series of announcements focusing on AI, including digital human microservices, NIM for model deployment, and supercharged Ethernet networking. The company is collaborating with the computer industry to build AI factories and data centers, and bringing AI assistants to GeForce RTX AI PCs, highlighting its pervasive role in advancing AI across various industries like robotics, healthcare, and industrial digitalization.

title: Soluna Cloud Secures Deal with San Francisco Compute Company to Deliver Custom AI Cloud Solutions
summary: Soluna Cloud has secured a Master Services Agreement with San Francisco Compute Company (SF Compute) to provide custom AI cloud solutions. Soluna will supply 80 to 120 Nvidia H100 GPUs for SF Compute's real-time compute trading platform, potentially generating $2.466 million in revenue over one year. This collaboration marks SF Compute as the first customer from Soluna's strategic partnership with Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) GreenLake.

title: MicroStrategy’s $2 billion Bitcoin buy is largest since 2020
summary: MicroStrategy Inc. has made its largest Bitcoin purchase since 2020, acquiring approximately 27,200 BTC for around $2.03 billion between October 31 and November 10. This brings the company's total Bitcoin holdings to about 279,420 BTC, valued at approximately $24 billion based on recent record prices. title: Pure Storage CEO Giancarlo: Pure Storage Platform Is Built For AI
summary: Pure Storage CEO Charles Giancarlo discusses how the Pure platform is designed to integrate AI and security, allowing enterprises to use existing data for analytics and AI without specialized environments. Giancarlo also highlights the competitive landscape and the strategic shift to position Pure Storage as a platform rather than just individual storage arrays, requiring a new approach to sales and channel engagement.

title: Jabil Acquires Mikros Technologies to Support Demand for Liquid Cooling in AI Data Centers
summary: Jabil Inc. has acquired Mikros Technologies LLC, a leader in liquid cooling solutions, to enhance its thermal management capabilities for AI data centers and other high-power density systems. The acquisition, completed on October 1st, will allow Jabil to address the growing demand for efficient cooling in industries such as artificial intelligence, energy storage, and electric vehicles. Mikros Technologies' proprietary microchannel liquid cooling designs will complement Jabil's existing data center solutions.

title: Soluna Unleashes First Batch of NVIDIA GPUs, Targeting $80 Million Revenue Over Three Years
summary: Soluna Holdings, Inc. has secured a $12.5 million credit facility for its new subsidiary, Soluna Cloud, Inc., to launch NVIDIA H100 GPU-based services. Soluna Cloud aims to provide enterprise-grade Generative AI solutions starting as early as July 2024.

summary: ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott announced new AI technologies and expanded partnerships with Nvidia and Cognizant, leveraging their Q3 earnings to position themselves as a leading AI company. The company also introduced Workflow Data Fabric to unify enterprise data and enhance workflow automation, aligning with their financial success which saw beats on revenue and earnings projections for Q3 2024.

summary: KeyBanc analyst John Vinh provided a mixed outlook for the semiconductor sector, with Nvidia and AMD showing strong performance and positive catalysts. Broadcom's stable outlook is tempered by potential future competition from Apple.

summary: Cadence Design Systems, Inc. announced its new Palladium Z3 Emulation and Protium X3 FPGA Prototyping systems, designed to accelerate verification and software development for complex SoCs. These systems offer over twice the capacity and are 1.5 times faster than previous generations, supporting advanced applications like generative AI, mobile, and automotive. The Palladium Z3 features a custom emulation processor and domain-specific apps, while the Protium X3 provides faster bring-up times for software validation, with both systems supporting massive gate designs up to 48 billion.

title: SoundHound AI Reports Record Third Quarter Revenue, Up 89%, Exceeding $25 Million; Raises Outlook
summary: SoundHound AI reported record third-quarter revenue of $25.1 million, an 89% increase year-over-year, and exceeded expectations. The company also announced an increased revenue outlook for both 2024 and 2025, driven by significant diversification in customer base and expansion into new verticals like financial services, healthcare, and insurance. Keyvan Mohajer, CEO of SoundHound AI, highlighted the company's strong position in conversational AI, attributing success to strong technology, vertical integrations, and proprietary software.

title: Nvidia shares jump 4% as the AI boom fuels another blockbuster quarter and better-than-expected forecast
summary: Nvidia reported another strong quarter, exceeding revenue and earnings expectations, driven by the ongoing AI boom. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the diversification of AI adoption beyond hyperscalers into various industries and sovereign AI initiatives.

summary: Alphabet has announced its first-ever quarterly dividend of $0.20 per share, payable on June 17 to shareholders of record as of June 10. summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and founder Bill Gates will meet with leaders of Samsung, SK Hynix, LG, and SK Telecom at the MS CEO Summit 2024 in May to discuss strengthening AI partnerships. The meetings aim to explore joint development of AI chips, cooperation in AI technology for consumer electronics, and business tie-ups in 5G telecommunications and cloud sectors. summary: Super Micro Computer shares surged 12.2% after the AI server company filed its delayed financial results by the Nasdaq's deadline, regaining compliance with filing requirements. Super Micro plans to hire more accounting and audit employees and upgrade IT systems to address these issues.

summary: Nvidia reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings, beating Wall Street expectations, with revenue up 78% year-over-year due to high demand for its AI-accelerating GPUs. summary: ZoomInfo's CEO, Henry Schuck, is buying more company stock after an earnings report caused shares to surge over 20%. summary: NVIDIA reported record financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2025, driven by strong demand for its Data Center products, particularly for Blackwell AI supercomputers. NVIDIA also provided an optimistic outlook for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, highlighting continued advancements and partnerships across various sectors including AI, Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive, and Robotics.

summary: Super Micro Computer successfully filed its delayed financial results just before the Nasdaq deadline, leading to a 22% surge in its stock during extended trading. summary: Foresight Autonomous Holdings Ltd. has integrated NVIDIA Jetson Orin computing platforms into its 3D perception technologies, expanding its focus from autonomous vehicles to uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). This collaboration utilizes both Jetson Orin Nano and Jetson AGX Orin to enhance performance, energy efficiency, and real-time data processing for diverse applications. The integration allows Foresight's systems to deliver advanced AI and GPU capabilities for improved environmental perception in challenging conditions.

summary: Sify Infinit Space launched its AI-Hub Data Centre in Lucknow to bolster northern India's data infrastructure. This initiative supports Uttar Pradesh's goal of becoming a data center hub and aligns with Sify's investment strategy and their recent certification as Nvidia's co-location partner.

summary: NVIDIA's Earth-2 platform introduces CorrDiff, a generative AI weather model that significantly enhances forecast precision for the continental U.S., down to a kilometer scale. summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) reported strong fourth-quarter results with growth in client and data center revenue, though its AI GPU growth forecast was disappointing compared to competitor Nvidia. Morningstar has cut its fair value estimate for AMD to $140 per share from $160 due to less optimism about AI GPU growth, but still considers the stock undervalued. The company holds a narrow economic moat based on intangible assets in chip design and expects significant long-term growth, particularly in the data center segment for AI applications.

title: Applied Digital Jumps On $375M SMBC Deal, Hood Stake – Retail Sentiment Improves
summary: Applied Digital (APLD) surged over 12% following a $375 million financing deal with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) for its Ellendale HPC campus. The stock also benefited from filings showing Hood River Capital Management acquired a 7.17% stake and Nvidia maintained its investment. This news significantly boosted retail sentiment on Stocktwits, moving it from bearish to neutral.

title: Report: Arm to build its own chips, and Meta is first in line to buy them
summary: Arm Holdings Plc. reportedly plans to design and build its own server CPUs, with Meta Platforms Inc. lined up as a first customer, marking a significant shift from its traditional licensing model. This move, driven by the lucrative AI chip market, could put Arm in direct competition with its existing licensees, potentially alienating customers but offering substantial new revenue streams. Analysts highlight both the immense opportunity in AI and the risks of disrupting established customer relationships.

title: Direxion Launches 2 Leveraged AMD ETFs Amid AI Chip Race
summary: Direxion has launched two new leveraged ETFs, Direxion Daily AMD Bull 2X Shares (AMUU) and Direxion Daily AMD Bear 1X Shares (AMDD), offering traders concentrated exposure to Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock. This move comes as AMD expands its presence in the artificial intelligence and data center markets, aiming to challenge Nvidia's dominance. The ETFs are designed for short-term trading due to their high-risk nature.

title: DeepSeek Shows There Is No Longer One “AI Trade,” but Many
summary: Recent developments from Chinese company DeepSeek, particularly its R1 model which uses fewer expensive chips, are signaling a new phase in AI investing. Fund managers now anticipate greater divergence among AI players, with potential benefits for companies like Broadcom and Marvell due to a shift towards more efficient chips. While efficiency gains could impact demand for some hardware, the overall growth in AI applications is expected to compensate, benefiting key players like Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor.

title: Solid Earnings Reflect Cirrus Logic's (NASDAQ:CRUS) Strength As A Business
summary: Cirrus Logic's recent strong earnings are supported by its impressive free cash flow. The company's accrual ratio of -0.11 indicates that its free cash flow of US$457m significantly exceeded its statutory profit of US$305.1m for the year ending December 2024. Additionally, its earnings per share have grown by 28% annually over the past three years, suggesting strong underlying business performance.

title: Digihost to Develop HPC and AI-Tier Data Centers
summary: Digihost Technology Inc. announced the formation of US Data Centers, Inc. (USDC), a new subsidiary focused on developing high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI)-focused data centers. USDC's first project will transform Digihost's existing site in Columbiana, Alabama, into a two-phase, 55 MW Tier 3 data center with an estimated total capital expenditure of $440 million. This strategic investment aims to meet the escalating demand for AI-driven computing power and cloud services.

title: Supermicro forecasts crazy revenue growth for fiscal 2026, boosting its stock
summary: Super Micro Computer Inc. saw its stock jump 9% after forecasting at least $40 billion in revenue for fiscal 2026, driven by demand for its AI hardware and direct-liquid cooling technology. This ambitious projection significantly exceeded Wall Street expectations, despite the company also revising down its fiscal 2025 guidance and facing scrutiny over financial irregularities and an ongoing Justice Department probe. The company is actively working to finalize its financial results to meet a critical February 25 deadline set by financial regulators.

title: Super Micro's roller coaster continues into earnings with 59% stock pop in past week
summary: Super Micro's stock has surged 59% in the past week, driven by strong AI market demand and significant capital spending forecasts from major tech companies. This follows a volatile 2024, which saw the stock drop significantly due to governance concerns and delayed financial reports. The upcoming earnings report is seen as a crucial test for the company to regain investor confidence amidst skepticism from analysts.

title: Digihost to Develop High-Performance Computing and AI-Tier
summary: Digihost Technology Inc. announced the formation of US Data Centers, Inc., a new subsidiary dedicated to developing high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI)-focused data centers. Their first project involves transforming an existing site in Columbiana, Alabama, into a 55 MW Tier 3 data center with an estimated total capital expenditure of $440 million, planned for completion by Q1 2027. This strategic investment aims to meet the escalating demand for AI-driven computing power and cloud services.

title: F5 targets AI-era IT challenges with ADC 3.0 reference architectures
summary: F5 Inc. has unveiled its new ADC 3.0 framework, a set of reference architectures and strategic partnerships designed to address the challenges of securely deploying and managing AI applications in complex hybrid and multicloud IT environments. This initiative responds to the increasing adoption of AI apps (75% of enterprises) and aims to simplify application delivery while enhancing security against emerging threats like model theft and data poisoning. F5 is collaborating with companies like Nvidia Corp. and NetApp Inc. to provide the necessary tools and infrastructure for the immense data processing and security demands of AI workloads.

title: CEO of Canada’s Celestica sells $130-million of shares, cashing in on Nvidia-style gains during AI boom
summary: Celestica's CEO, Rob Mionis, sold $130-million in company shares amidst an AI boom that saw the company's stock price surge over 1,000 percent, akin to Nvidia's growth. Other top executives also sold shares, totaling $212-million, as Celestica's profits jumped significantly due to its critical role in providing storage and network switches for AI-driven data centers, making hyperscalers a major portion of its revenue. This financial success comes after decades of languishing stock prices, with the company finding new life through its high-end manufacturing for the AI sector.

title: NXP buys Kinara for $307M to power AI workloads at the network edge
summary: Dutch chipmaker NXP Semiconductors N.V. has acquired California-based startup Kinara Inc. for $307 million to bolster its presence in AI workloads at the network edge. This acquisition, following two other recent deals, aims to strengthen NXP's Industrial & IoT group and expand its AI capabilities, especially after a period of declining revenues. Kinara's neural processing units, like the Ara-1 and Ara-2 NPUs, are expected to provide NXP with viable edge AI products and help diversify its chip business.

title: Bit Digital, Inc. Secures New Multi-Year Colocation Agreement with a Leader in AI Hardware
summary: Bit Digital, Inc. (Nasdaq: BTBT) has secured a multi-year colocation agreement with a leading AI hardware innovator. Through its rebranded HPC business, WhiteFiber, the company will provide 5 MW of built-to-suit data center infrastructure for five years, with the contract expected to commence in mid-2025 at an Enovum data center. This partnership highlights Bit Digital's capability to deliver high-performance colocation solutions for next-generation AI workloads.

title: U.S. Retracts Tariff Waiver for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
summary: The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has retracted a tariff waiver for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and canceled its Validated End-User program. This means TSMC and similar companies will now require a special license to export chipmaking technology to China, aiming to level the playing field with U.S.-owned fabricators. President Trump also announced new tariffs on semiconductors from companies that do not produce them domestically, encouraging U.S. manufacturing.
